The GHBO will provide enterprise-wide leadership across business management, portfolio and program governance, financial planning, vendor and third-party oversight, market data, Finance Technology, communications and the Office of the COO. The role will establish the operating cadence, governance, management information and cross-functional coordination needed to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes. Working across Investments, Institutional, Cash, Global Client Coverage Group, the Chief Business Office, Finance, Technology, Data, Marketing and corporate functions, the GHBO will lead a globally distributed organization and influence senior stakeholders across multiple regions.

jobs.title: FaST Product Install Engineer
jobs.description_text:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.



What You'll Do

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

Do you want to work on some of the most complex and cutting edge technologies in a dynamic environment with good career opportunities, if so, KLA is searching for Engineers to join our installation team in Europe securing proper tool installation at KLA customer sites & completing all activities required to ensure a KLA tool functions accurately!

Our Installation engineers are a critical part of our new product deployment projects while traveling to some of the most advanced factories in the world they work in multicultural teams to meet our project commitments.

Key responsibilities include:          

  • Hold pre-installation meetings with the customer to scope customer unique requirements. Create a plan of action to measure/confirm/satisfy unique customer needs. Validate deliverables with customers.

  • Install tool at customer site to meet KLA specifications, through system testing according to procedures. This includes but is not limited to: light source and optical integration and precision alignment; wafer handler robot integration and teaching; camera and collection optics alignment and calibration; system-level calibrations and verification; performance testing for sensitivity and repeatability; stability and cleanliness testing; applications verification and product wafer validation.

  • Solving complex system issues in a timely manner, using abstract thought, data analysis, seven-step problem-solving methodology, and other available tools.

  • Management of critical issues across customers and regions.

  • After system testing, meet with the customer to facilitate verification of the tool performance, during which the validation of the tool is performed, to ensure it is properly functioning.

  • Management of customer satisfaction through pre-activity meetings, routine update meetings, escalation meetings, post-activity meetings, and warranty meetings.

  • Perform install/customer-focused application testing to approve the operational quality of the tool.

  • Provide new product installation training to worldwide customer support engineering.

KLA offers a challenging and multinational environment at the forefront of high technology and a highly competitive package. As a global organization, the KLA family allows you to build a career within and avail of a variety of opportunities across our technologies and factories around the globe. Joining KLA could be one of the best decisions you will ever make!

As an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable law.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Technical degree/diploma in engineering, mechanical, electrical, electronic engineering or equivalent work experience.
  • 2-3 years semiconductor industry work experience is a bonus.
  • Panel of competencies in optical, mechanic, electronic, lithography, metrology, and laser technology – is desirable.
  • Good level technical & analytical skills, ability to understand and solve problems in software and electronic, optic, mechanical, electro-mechanical or electro-optical systems.
  • Knowledge of computer theory, operating systems i.e. MS Windows.
  • Good interpersonal/communication skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and work to project deadlines.
  • Available to travel internationally.
  • Domestic and international travel, including to the United States, will be required as part of this role

About KLA

We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.


Use of AI Statement 

At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset.



We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees.


KLA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

  • Deep understanding of:
    • Device matching
    • Parasitic effects
    • Shielding and isolation techniques
    • Reliability and ESD considerations
    • Power distribution and substrate management

  • Strong scripting/programming experience, with demonstrated ability to develop and maintain engineering automation solutions.
  • Experience with Cadence SKILL programming for Virtuoso-based layout automation, productivity utilities, design checks, or flow integration.
  • Experience with Python for engineering automation, data processing, workflow integration, or tool development.
  • Working knowledge of Shell/Bash and/or Tcl for design-flow automation and EDA tool integration.
  • Ability to translate analog layout knowledge and repetitive engineering workflows into robust, reusable automation used by other engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing engineering automation deployed to multiple users.
  • Experience with analog layout generators and parameterized cell development.
  • Experience with, or interest in, analog placement and routing automation.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted engineering workflows.

The Business

ADI’s Data Center & Energy business is the key provider of power solutions serving the breadth of ADI’s end markets. As part of a long term sustainable growth plan, ADI is expanding its power team in Ireland, supporting the development of highly integrated power solutions. Data Center & Energy BU will present the successful candidate a great opportunity for continuous career development as part of a highly motivated and supportive worldwide engineering team.



The Team

The Power Controller (PWC) Design team has the mission to expand ADI’s current portfolio of power devices, innovating through, for example, the addition of new smart control features and integrated digital configurability. The team is growing its power solutions to complement the existing mixed-signal products and advance toward cutting-edge technologies.

The PWC organization is looking for a Principal Engineer, Analog Design Engineering, with deep expertise in power DC-DC converters. The candidate will lead analog IC design and technical project execution, working with digital design, verification, layout, test, and silicon evaluation teams to deliver power-controller products into production.



Responsibilities include, but not limited to:

  • Provide technical leadership for analog and mixed-signal IC design of power DC-DC converter controllers, from architecture and feasibility through production release.

  • Apply deep circuit-design expertise to optimize stability, transient response, efficiency, accuracy, noise, and robustness across process, voltage, and temperature.
  • Lead system and transistor-level design reviews; establish specifications, simulation plans, design margins, and sign-off criteria for key analog blocks.
  • Own technical delivery of multiple IC design projects, coordinating priorities, schedules, design decisions, risks, and dependencies across engineering teams.
  • Guide schematic design, behavioral modeling, mixed-signal integration, and verification of analog-digital interfaces and converter operating modes.
  • Work closely with digital designers to share system-level requirements, agree on the desired behavior, and review the delivered digital solutions.
  • Partner with layout engineers on matching, parasitics, isolation, power routing, electromigration, ESD, and latch-up to achieve robust physical implementation.
  • Direct silicon bring-up and laboratory characterization; correlate measurements with simulations, resolve design issues, and support qualification and production ramp.
  • Work with product, applications, and test teams to translate customer and system needs into product requirements and support production test and field debug.
  • Lead technical reviews and communicate design status, trade-offs, risks, and mitigation plans clearly to project stakeholders and senior management.
  • Mentor analog designers, develop team capability, and promote reusable circuits, rigorous design practices, and effective cross-team collaboration.

 


Minimum Qualifications:

  • BSEE (or equivalent) + 12+ years of relevant experience in analog IC design; advanced degree a plus.
  • Experience in high-voltage analog circuit design
  • Solid foundation in semiconductor physics
  • Proven technical leadership of multiple ICs design from concept through tape-out, including ownership of verification plans, sign-off readiness and laboratory validation.
  • Expertise in precision analog blocks, current sensing, gate drivers, fault protection, and digitally configurable power systems.
  • Deep hands-on knowledge of transistor-level analog circuit design and power DC-DC converter architectures, control loops, and power-management circuits.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership of engineering teams and complex IC projects, including planning, design reviews, mentoring, and cross-functional coordination.
  • Strong expertise in analog simulation, including stability analysis, PVT and mismatch verification, layout-aware design, and mixed-signal simulations.
  • Good knowledge of IC reliability, ESD and latch-up prevention, electromigration, and production test considerations.
  • Proficiency with Cadence analog design tools, SPICE simulation, and mixed-signal design and verification flows.
  • Experience of System-level analysis using tools such as SIMPLIS, MATLAB/Simulink or Mathcad.
  • Ability to communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, project status, and risks effectively to engineers and management

Preferred Qualifications & Experience:

  • Experience in behavioural modeling using languages such as SystemVerilog.
  • Experience delivering multiphase buck or high-performance DC-DC converter controllers into production.

  • Define component qualification requirements and derating guidelines.
  • Support environmental, EMC, safety, and reliability testing activities.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable industry, customer, and regulatory requirements.
  • Drive corrective actions for component-related failures and field issues.

Manufacturing & Sustaining Engineering

  • Support transition from development to production.
  • Resolve manufacturing-related component issues.
  • Provide guidance on process improvements and manufacturability.

Experience

jobs.description_text:
About Analog Devices

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.

          

Solutions and Tool Specialist – Functional Safety

About the Role

Safety-critical semiconductor products are growing across every market ADI serves. The Functional Safety Office (FSO) is a global team responsible for independent safety confirmation at the highest integrity levels per ISO 26262, and the tooling and infrastructure that supports that work needs to scale with the portfolio.

This role puts you at the center of that challenge. You will build reusable analysis infrastructure — starting with Medini Analyze component libraries — support the development of training content, and work across multiple product families and design types rather than being embedded in a single program. You will gain broad cross-portfolio exposure to how safety-critical semiconductor products are developed.

This role offers a structured path into functional safety — with mentoring from experienced Safety Specialists, progressive project exposure, and the opportunity to build the tooling infrastructure that shapes how safety engineering scales across ADI. You are not expected to arrive as a functional safety expert. You are expected to arrive as an engineer with a solid foundation in semiconductor product development or quality engineering who wants to build tools, tool interfaces, reusable assets and workflows that improve engineering execution.

Why This Team

The FSO operates as ADI's independent safety authority, working across business units and product families rather than within a single design group. The team is global and high-impact — the tooling and methods you help build here will be used across every safety-critical product ADI ships. You will gain exposure to a breadth of product architectures and safety challenges that few individual contributor roles in the industry offer.

Job Responsibilities:

Support, develop and maintain reusable component libraries in Medini Analyze for safety analysis (FMEDA, FTA, dependent failure analysis) across ADI product families, working alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists to ensure technical accuracy and standards compliance.

Work with the FSO team and BU teams to standardize analysis templates and modeling patterns, and translate product-family-specific safety architectures into reusable, parameterized components that improve consistency and reduce setup time for new assessments.

Support the development of role-based training content for common safety activities including FMEDA execution, safety case construction, and safety requirements writing.

Engage with tool vendors such as Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) on capability evaluation, feature requests, and user community activities.

Develop functional safety domain expertise through structured mentoring and progressive project exposure, contributing to confirmation reviews and safety assessments as competence develops.

Who You Will Work With:

Day-to-day: You will work alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists around the world, who provide technical direction and mentoring on safety analysis and Medini.

Across the FSO: You will collaborate with Functional Safety Managers and Safety Specialists globally to understand where enablement assets have the highest impact.

Engineering teams: You will work with Design Engineers across business units who are the consumers of the tools, templates, and training content you help build.

Tool vendors: You will participate in vendor engagements with Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) and others on tool capabilities and integration.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in semiconductor design engineering, quality engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Solid understanding of semiconductor product development processes and lifecycle.
  • Experience with structured analytical methods used in product development such as FMEA, design verification, characterization, simulation, or reliability analysis.
  • Experience building reusable technical assets such as component libraries, parameterized templates, structured analysis workflows, or design tools.
  • Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate complex methods into clear, usable guidance for engineering teams.
  • Self-directed work style suited to a globally distributed team spanning multiple countries and time zones.
  • Willingness to travel approximately 10%, primarily to ADI sites in Europe and the US.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with safety analysis methods specifically (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA) including failure mode identification and classification.
  • Experience with Synopsys-Ansys Medini Analyze or comparable safety analysis tools (Isograph, ReliaSoft, APIS IQ, Safety Office).
  • Familiarity with functional safety standards (ISO 26262, IEC 61508) at a conceptual level. Direct certification is not required.
  • Experience developing training content, structured knowledge management systems, or technical curricula.
  • Familiarity with automotive quality standards such as IATF 16949 or development process standards such as ASPICE.

Functional safety is one of the fastest-growing disciplines in semiconductor engineering, and this role gives you a structured way in — with mentoring, real project exposure, and the chance to build infrastructure that engineering teams across ADI rely on. If you've been looking for a role with more cross-portfolio visibility and a longer lever than single-program work, we'd like to hear from you.

We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.


Job Description

The Associate Director leads the S2P Contracting COE (“S2P CCOE”), reports to the Sr. Director, S2P COE, and implements Global Procurement’s contracting strategy.  The role manages and develops a team of Contract Managers supporting Global Procurement and owns the Master Procurement Template (MPT) contract inventory, Procurement’s Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) processes, and contract knowledge management.  The role works closely with partners such as Lilly Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity, Corporate Risk Management, Tax, and Import/Export to manage risk through approved negotiation playbooks, keeps templates current with new laws and regulations, and ensures that CLM AI Redline Models reflect MPT inventory changes and CLM processes meet the needs of the S2P organization.  The role also provides contracting subject matter expertise to S2P COE colleagues.


Key Responsibilities:


Personnel Management and Development

  • Lead, supervise, coach, and develop the S2P Contracting COE team to deliver on its mission. This includes a mix of direct reports and an M1 supervisor.
  • Attract, develop, and retain a diverse team, including onboarding new staff.
  • Model Lilly values and foster an environment where results are recognized and team members feel comfortable speaking up and sharing ideas.
  • Hold regular development conversations: share feedback, identify strengths and growth areas, coach, support mentoring, and manage performance.
  • Manage and forecast team resource needs so projects are completed on time.

Master Procurement Templates

  •  Own the MPT contract inventory.
  • Oversee change control for new and updated MPT clauses, templates, and playbook guidance.
  • Manage and oversee ad hoc specialty projects, such as amending large volumes of contracts to comply with applicable law or internal policy updates.
  • Represent MPT standards and the negotiation playbook in audits.
  • Partner with cross-functional and Procurement colleagues to identify needed changes to the MPT inventory and Work Order Templates.
  • Analyze frequently negotiated terms and recommend MPT updates to Lilly Legal/SMEs and Procurement leadership.

Contract Training

  •  Partner with S2P Learning & Development to build role-specific CLM and MPT training and onboard Global Procurement on their use.
  • Create and maintain onboarding and training resources and materials for the S2P Contracting COE.
  • Oversee MPT-related content on the Supplier Resources Portal on Lilly.com. 

Contract Lifecycle Management Program

  • Partner closely with leaders across Procurement, IBU Procurement and Lilly Legal to define and implement a shared CLM program strategy, driving progress to agreed budget and timelines.
  • Report progress, proactively identify risk, and escalate in a timely manner to leadership.
  • Lead pre-implementation discovery efforts with project team to identify gaps, elicit requirements, develop process maps, and identify contract management reporting needs, KPIs and SLAs.
  • Ensure the CLM solution and training program comply with Lilly policies and procedures.
  • Partner with Tech@Lilly to guide the CLM vendor on requirements, development, legacy contract migration, integrations, and validation testing, and to manage the vendor relationship for performance, security, and compliance.
  • Benchmark CLM practices and recommend opportunities for innovation and improvement. 
  • Lead project team as the contracting SME to deliver program key objectives to meet Lilly’s tactical and strategic objectives inclusive of:
    • Transformation of Procurement’s contracting process and use of CLM technology solutions.

jobs.description_text:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely. 

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

The Role

Clio is building an agentic Security Operations Center. Instead of staffing a room of analysts to watch dashboards, we're building the AI-driven system that does the watching: it triages alerts, investigates, and takes the first response action, so the humans on the team spend their time on the work that needs a human. Our goal is to automate every event we can, and we mean every event.


We're looking for the manager who builds both the Blue Team's software and the team itself. This is an engineering leadership role first. The team writes software: detection pipelines, automated response, the agents, and the integrations that tie them into Clio's products and infrastructure. You'll lead that team, set its technical direction, and stay close enough to the code to review it and contribute. Beyond leading, you'll get into the codebase and make changes in the agentic SOC and Clio's core applications, accelerated by Claude and Codex.


You won't be working alone. Clio's Red Team finds and exploits weaknesses; the Threat Intelligence function tracks who is targeting us and how. The Blue Team takes what both of them learn and turns it into defenses that hold: hardened infrastructure, hardened product, and detection that catches the next attempt automatically.



Building the Team

As you onboard, one of the first tasks will be building out the team. We care much more about finding the right people than filling seats quickly, and you'll own that search: defining what great looks like, interviewing, and selling the work to people who have plenty of options.


The people we want are builders who are curious about security, or security people who build. You'll set the culture for a small, senior-leaning team that ships, owns the results, and makes its work visible to the rest of the company.



A Day in the Life

  • AI-assisted code writing in core Clio applications to add observability to the system
  • Sitting with the Red Team after an exercise to turn their findings into detections and fixes, then confirming the fixes hold on retest
  • Reading a new threat intel brief on a technique being used against SaaS companies, and deciding which part of the infrastructure to harden first
  • Working with a product engineering team to ensure incoming changes do not weaken the security posture of the application
  • Spotting a spike in suspicious account activity, and asking why a human noticed it before the automation did
  • Interviewing a candidate, then writing up honest feedback the same afternoon
  • Reviewing PRs from SOC agents, and developers from engineering teams at Clio to ensure changes are securely implemented


What You'll Do

Build the agentic SOC

  • Lead the design and build of an AI-driven SOC that monitors, triages, investigates, and responds with as little human toil as possible
  • Treat every manual alert-handling step as a candidate for automation, and measure how much of the queue the system closes on its own
  • Own detection engineering: detection-as-code, testing, tuning
  • Make sure the automation is trustworthy: clear guardrails on what it can do unattended, audit trails for what it did, and a human escalation path when it isn't sure
  • Work with the wider security team on incident response when something real happens, and feed what you learn back into the system

Harden against new adversary techniques

  • Work with Threat Intelligence to turn new tactics, techniques, and procedures into concrete hardening work and detection coverage
  • Prioritize infrastructure hardening across cloud, identity, and endpoints based on observed attacker behaviour rather than benchmarks alone

Harden Clio's products

  • Work directly on the core security functionality of Clio's fleet of products, alongside the product engineering teams that own them
  • Push security controls into the platform itself, so every product team gets them without having to rebuild them

Close the loop with the Red Team

  • Partner with the Red Team to find vulnerabilities, fix them, and verify the fixes
  • Run exercises to measure detection coverage against real attack paths, and close the gaps they expose

Detect and stop product abuse

  • Build automated detection for abuse of Clio's products: account takeover, fraud, scripted misuse, and patterns we haven't named yet
  • Automate the response as well as the detection, so confirmed abuse is contained without waiting for someone to notice
  • Work closely with SecDev to build preventative code generation paths, agent.md guides, and create pre-commit hooks

Lead the team

  • Hire, grow, and retain a team of engineers
  • Set clear direction and priorities, and make the team's progress visible to security leadership and the wider company
  • Help define how the team scales toward follow-the-sun coverage

What You Bring

  • Strong software development skills. We want you to build the software and have a direct impact on it
  • Experience leading engineers, as a people manager or a tech lead who has grown into the role
  • Hands-on security experience: secure development, and finding and fixing vulnerabilities
  • Comfort making decisions about automation and AI where the cost of being wrong is a locked out lawyer that can sue us for free, and designing systems that fail safely
  • Clear communication with engineers, leadership, and partner teams

Bonus Points

  • You started in the trenches (SOC analyst, incident responder) and moved into engineering. We know this path is rare, and we'd love to hear from you if it's yours!
  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs or agentic systems in production
  • Detection engineering experience with a SIEM, SOAR, or detection-as-code pipeline
  • Experience with fraud, anti-abuse, or trust and safety systems
  • Cloud security and infrastructure hardening experience (AWS, identity providers, endpoint tooling)
  • A recognized security certification or equivalent track record such as CISSP, GIAC/GCIH, OSCP, CREST
  • Experience running or planning a follow-the-sun or on-call security function

What you will find here:


Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include: 

  • Competitive, equitable salary
  • Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions to be in office minimum twice per week. (Find your Hub)
  • 25 days holiday + bank holidays
  • Private Healthcare with Life Insurance & Critical Illness cover
  • Pension contribution
  • Professional development and growth options
  • Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years
The expected salary range for this role is £104,000 to £156,000 GBP. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. As General Manager, UK & Ireland, you will own the strategy, the revenue, and the team for the region. You will set the plan, build the leadership bench to deliver it, and be the face of Clio to solicitors, barristers, law firms, industry bodies, and partners across both markets. This role sits at the intersection of product execution and regional partnership, and it suits someone who thrives in complexity, builds for diverse users, and gets into the weeds.

Our market opportunity is rare in its scale and powered by a strong business model, first-rate investors and advisors, and a global product management team (if we do say so ourselves). Clio is growing rapidly, and Product Managers here grow their scope as we open new markets.

Speaking of Product at Clio, we have worked hard to develop an excellent product management culture with empowered PMs who carry real influence across the organization. Our team brings together seasoned professionals from a diverse set of product backgrounds. Clio invests heavily in developing Product Managers, growing leaders, and in the broader Product communities in which we operate.

What you'll work on:

As a Senior Product Manager, and in conjunction with your Development and Design counterparts (your triad), you will drive successful outputs and outcomes across Clio's portfolio in France.

End to End Portfolio Ownership:

  • You own Clio's product portfolio and customer experience in France end to end, from first touch through onboarding, daily practice management, billing, and support. Where a gap sits in a product another team owns, you own getting it closed.

  • You are accountable for the quality of Clio's customer experience in France as a whole, rather than for a single feature area. Your measure of success is whether a lawyer in France can run their practice on Clio without hitting a wall that a lawyer in North America would not hit.

  • You maintain a single, current view of what breaks today, what is missing, and what we have committed for France, and you make that view legible to leadership before leadership asks for it.

Product Leadership and Execution:

  • Working from the overarching strategy set by your Senior Director, Product Management, you will develop a roadmap in conjunction with your peers that moves our business forward, and evangelize it throughout the company.

  • You will own the delivery of features in the roadmap while also ensuring they deliver on the desired business outcome.

  • Drive product readiness for the French market, including localization, multi-lingual support, regulatory requirements, and market-specific workflows.

Speed and Iteration Toward a Clear Vision:

  • You set a clear vision for what Clio looks like in France, then ship toward it in weeks rather than quarters. We expect a first customer-visible change within your first 90 days.

  • You will make decisions with imperfect information, put something in front of customers, and correct from what you learn. We aim to validate with real customers before building at scale, however there are scenarios where a regulatory deadline sets the date. In those cases we will commit to the date and narrow the scope rather than move the date.

  • You parallelize. When a workstream can run alongside another, you run it alongside, and you say what serializing would cost in weeks when you choose to serialize.

Local Legal Market Understanding:

  • You understand how lawyers in France actually work: how French civil law shapes a firm's structure, how matters progress through the local courts, how the profession sets and regulates fees, what the Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres require of a practitioner, and where local practice diverges from common law practice.

  • You track the regulatory surface that touches our product, including French electronic invoicing under the Factur-X and PDP regime, TVA, and Conseil National des Barreaux professional rules, and you translate it into requirements our central teams can build against.

  • You build and maintain direct relationships with practitioners, bar associations, and local partners, and you serve as the company's source of truth on what the French legal profession needs.

System Design and Technical Fluency:

  • You can read and reason about how we built our platform: where our data models carry a country assumption, how the model represents currency, tax, payments, and locale, and what a change to one of those costs downstream.

  • You can hold a design discussion with engineering about cardinality, extensibility, and migration, and leave with a shared decision.

  • You can tell a problem that needs a local configuration from a problem that needs a platform capability, and you argue for the platform capability when it is the right answer.

AI Native Working Style:

  • You work AI-first by default. You use AI for customer research synthesis, competitive and regulatory analysis, requirements drafting, data querying, and prototyping, and you can show how it changed your throughput.

  • You build your own working systems. You are comfortable writing prompts, chaining tools, and standing up a lightweight agent or script to remove repetitive work from your week.

  • You bring judgment to it. You know which AI output needs verification against a primary source, particularly on regulatory and legal questions, and you verify it.

Influencing Central Teams:

  • Central teams build the platform that France depends on, and their leadership sets their goals, metrics, and roadmap without France in them. Your job is to quantify the case for France well enough that it wins a place on that roadmap.

  • You will build the business case in the currency that team's leadership measures it on, name the tradeoff you are asking them to make, and find the version of the ask that serves their goal alongside yours.

  • You escalate on a stated trigger rather than on frustration. When merit alone does not win the ask, you bring your Senior Director a clear recommendation and the cost of inaction.

Cross-Functional Partnership:

  • Partner closely with cross-functional leaders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Operations to support the French market launch and growth.

  • Manage stakeholder relationships across a matrixed organization with clarity and diplomacy.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in French and in English. Clio operates in English, so English fluency is a requirement of the role rather than a preference.

  • 4-5 years of experience in product management

  • Working knowledge of the French legal market, including French civil law, how local firms operate, and the regulatory requirements that apply to them

  • Proven track record of independently taking multiple products or features from ideation to launch in a SaaS environment

  • Experience owning a product area end to end, including outcomes that depended on teams outside your own

  • Demonstrated expertise in localization and multi-lingual product development. This is a core requirement for the role.

  • Experience building or managing multilingual applications or internationalization projects, and expanding products to other countries and languages

  • Technical fluency sufficient to reason about system design, data models, and platform tradeoffs with engineering

  • A demonstrated AI-native working style, with specific examples of how you use AI in your product practice

  • Evidence of winning roadmap commitments from teams that do not report to you and that carry no accountability for your outcome

  • Exceptional attention to detail, so that no requirement or specification slips through the product development cycle

  • Outstanding organizational skills, capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously without compromising quality or timelines

  • Experience using data to inform decisions without succumbing to analysis paralysis

  • Genuine ability to put yourself in our customers' shoes and operate from a place of empathy

  • Experience working across time zones and cultures, with a customer-first approach

  • An entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in ambiguity

  • At least 2 or 3 failures under your belt, the learnings of which you can bring to Clio

  • Ability to work in a highly collaborative team without ego

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Serious bonus points if you:

  • Have prior experience in legal tech, or a strong understanding of the legal services market, including familiarity with legal practice management software and the needs of legal professionals

  • Have worked directly with Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres or comparable professional bodies

  • Worked previously in a regulated industry or with multi-product ecosystems

  • Have shipped against a regulatory deadline in France or another EU market

  • Successfully launched products in global markets

  • Have a track record of breaking down objectives into initiatives and delivering to customers at scale

  • Have built internal tooling or agents to support your own product practice

  • Demonstrable experience self-serving answers, insights, and data from a variety of data analytics tools

jobs.title: Senior Consultant – Public Sector Finance Transformation, Hybrid
jobs.description_text:
Deloitte is the world’s number one professional services firm and making an impact is more than what we do. It is why we are here. We bring challenge, curiosity and edge to every project, driving positive progress for our clients, our people, our communities and the planet. This purpose inspires us to work to the highest standards and to tackle the challenges that matter. Number one never stops challenging.

Joining us means becoming part of a Technology and Transformation team that brings challenge, curiosity and edge to every engagement. Working with leading technologies and exceptional people, you will deliver meaningful change for high profile local and international clients. You will help shape the future of digital transformation within a people first culture that is collaborative, innovative and welcoming. At Deloitte, the world’s number one professional services firm, you will tackle complex challenges in an environment where number one never stops challenging.


We offer a competitive starting salary of €55,000.00 for this role, with salary adjustments reflecting your experience level and expertise.
.

Why you'll enjoy this new opportunity?

 

At Deloitte, our purpose is to make an impact that matters. By joining our Government & Public Services (G&PS) team within the Finance Transformation practice, you'll work with government departments, public bodies and agencies on complex transformation challenges that directly affect how public services are funded, managed and delivered. You'll help finance leaders translate policy priorities and transformation ambitions into practical, sustainable improvements.

 

As a Senior Consultant, you'll take ownership of meaningful client workstreams across finance transformation. You'll combine structured problem-solving, strong project delivery and stakeholder management with practical finance technology, AI and automation capability to help public sector finance functions become more efficient, insight-led and digitally enabled.

 

Key skills and prior experience that align well with this position:

 

  • Experience delivering finance transformation projects in consulting or an in-house role, with exposure to areas such as finance strategy, service or operating model design, process improvement, organisational change, digital transformation or programme delivery.
  • A strong understanding of public sector policy, governance, structures and ways of working, ideally gained through assignments with government departments, agencies or wider public services.
  • Experience assessing and improving core finance processes such as Record-to-Report (R2R), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Order-to-Cash (O2C), planning, budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting and with the ability to map processes, analyse root causes and translate findings into practical recommendations.
  • Strong project delivery capability, including planning and managing workstreams, risks, issues, dependencies and deliverables, and working effectively across multidisciplinary client and Deloitte teams.
  • Strong issue-led problem-solving, analytical and communication skills, with the ability to turn complex evidence into clear insights, recommendations, business cases and client-ready presentations for senior stakeholders.
  • Fluent use of Microsoft Copilot, Claude and other AI productivity tools in day-to-day project work to improve efficiency and produce high-quality deliverables, including presentations, trackers, analysis and reporting.
  • Ability to identify and frame AI opportunities across finance processes, assess where AI can add value, shape clear use cases and articulate benefits to finance and public sector stakeholders.
  • Experience in finance technology design and implementation programmes including end to end project lifecycle with platforms including Oracle and SAP preferably.
  • A relevant third-level qualification. An accounting qualification such as ACA, ACCA or CIMA, and/or a programme/project management qualification, is desirable but not essential.

 

What type of work will I be doing?

 

  • Develop work plans and manage high-quality delivery across one or more project workstreams.
  • Assess current finance processes and operating models, identify gaps and inefficiencies, and design future-state processes, service delivery models and implementation roadmaps.
  • Support improvements across R2R, P2P, O2C, planning and budgeting, reporting, shared services and related finance capabilities, using process mapping, requirements gathering, root-cause analysis, maturity assessments and benchmarking where appropriate.
  • Assess and prioritise AI and automation opportunities in finance, build AI into future-state process and operating model designs and business cases, and help quantify expected benefits and implementation considerations.
  • Apply data, industry insight, technology and public sector context to evaluate options and develop evidence-based business cases and recommendations.
  • Present clear, evidence-based advice to client stakeholders and support delivery across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Manage day-to-day client relationships, engage confidently with senior stakeholders, raise risks early and support workshops, interviews and governance forums.
  • Coach junior colleagues and provide direction on client-facing and internal work.
  • Contribute to proposals and broad business development for Finance Transformation across the G&PS sector.

 

Who is the Hiring Manager?

 

The hiring manager is a leader within Deloitte's Finance Transformation and Government & Public Services practice, with experience helping public sector organisations deliver complex finance and technology-enabled transformation. They are committed to developing consulting talent, encouraging innovation and responsible use of emerging technology, and creating an environment where high-quality delivery, collaboration and measurable client impact are expected and supported.

 

Where is this role based?

 

This role is based in Dublin and operates on a flexible hybrid working model, combining Deloitte office, client-site and remote working as project delivery requires.

jobs.description_text:
Company:

Marsh

Description:

We currently have an exciting opportunity within our Marsh Investments International Limited Compliance Team. This role will be based in Dublin and is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.


Please note, this role will fall under the Central Bank of Ireland (“CBI”) Fitness and Probity Regime, and the successful candidate (subject to the completion of due diligence) will hold a CF2 role - Ensuring, controlling or monitoring compliance by a regulated financial service provider with its relevant obligations. As a CF2 role holder, you will also be subject to the Common Conduct Standards under the Individual Accountability Framework.


What can you expect:


Marsh Investments has experienced significant growth over the last 10 years and with a strong pipeline of activity, this looks set to continue for the foreseeable future. This growth has involved  new client on-boarding, as well as more recent inorganic growth across the broader Marsh Investments group, and has seen the business further enhance its product and service offering and its position in the market.


Marsh Investments’ Compliance Department protects Marsh’s reputation and provides advice to the Company. It understands, challenges and advises on the impact of regulation in our business, with the objective of:


  • Actively participating in business decisions to champion our clients’ interests
  • Collaborating with the business to position Compliance centrally in their daily work;
  • Ensuring securing client interests is at the centre of everything we do;
  • Cultivating and enhancing the compliance culture within Mercer;

The roleholder will report to a Senior Compliance Manager who reports to the MIIL Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) and be responsible for assisting in the oversight and management of regulatory and other risks in respect of Marsh’s Investments business in Ireland and other jurisdictions relevant to that business, including its branches in Germany and Sweden. 


We will rely on you to:


  • Support investment compliance monitoring activities for MIIL and the broader Marsh Investments business. 
  • Monitor investment restriction and guideline breaches arising in respect of the funds and client portfolios under management, including sustainability related commitments across the platform.
  • Perform reviews and consider potential investment vehicles against the relevant regulations and fund documentation in relation to the Mercer Funds and other portfolios.
  • Liaise with fund managers and client relationship managers in relation to investment issues on funds and portfolios under management.
  • Support regular liaison with the depositary of the funds under management, maintenance of logs and review of regulatory reports.
  • Monitor quarterly investment management questionnaires and oversight of due diligence of investment managers.
  • Assistance in the review of fund documentation ahead of launch and on an ongoing basis.
  • Roll out, tracking and review of quarterly employee declarations and oversight of the personal trading monitoring system.
  • Develop and maintain policies and procedures supporting a culture of integrity, risk management and excellence in the Investments business in Ireland.
  • Assist with the identification of potential risks and financial services compliance issues associated with new products, services and jurisdictions in the Investments business.
  • Prepare various reports for senior members of the Investment business (as needed).
  • Support the governance process relating to the Investments business and the entities that host this (most notably the Risk Committees and the Board).
  • Conduct periodic compliance monitoring assessments of the business and where necessary, any third party providers.
  • Developing and conducting periodic training for Investments personnel relating to regulated activities.
  • Assisting with the management of regulatory matters and compliance issues, including correspondence with regulators, overseeing regulatory examinations; implementation of new regulations etc

What you will need to have:


  • Highly motivated with a passion for compliance in the asset management/investment funds industry.
  • A broad understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to the operation of MIIL. This includes Irish (and EU) Investments regulation in particular MiFID and UCITS & AIFMD related to the funds and portfolios for which MIIL acts as Investment Manager.
  • Good knowledge of fund structures, different fund types and different assets class would be an advantage.
  • Minimum of three year’s investment compliance experience.
  • Takes initiative and ownership of responsibilities assigned.
  • Ability to prioritize activities while working on multiple tasks and achieve target deadlines.
  • Ability to work effectively within a small, fast growing team and assist in the development of that team.
  • Strong interpersonal skills to communicate with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
  • Fluent English essential.

What makes you stand out:


  • Fund Compliance experience particularly advantageous.
  • A current role in the Risk, Audit or Compliance group of an asset management/regulatory advisory firm would be valued.

Why join our team:


  • We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
  • We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can collaborate with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
  • Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities.

Description:

Marsh People and Investments (Marsh P&I) is the Health, Wealth and Career business of Marsh, a global professional services firm headquartered in New York. As the single accountable technology leader for Ireland, you will translate business and client priorities into a clear, prioritised technology roadmap and ensure that regional, global, local, vendor and squad-based teams deliver against agreed outcomes.

Job Description & Summary

As organisations adopt AI and advanced analytics, the quality, classification, and protection of data has become a critical business and security risk. PwC’s Cybersecurity & Privacy practice supports clients in establishing robust data risk and security foundations that enable secure AI adoption, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience.

As a Senior Associate, you will work on data risk, data protection, and AI enablement engagements, supporting clients to understand where their sensitive data lives, how it is used, and how it should be protected , particularly in the context AI-driven solutions.

This role is ideal for candidates with experience in data security, information protection, and data governance tooling who are interested in expanding into AI security and AI risk.

As a Senior Associate within our Cybersecurity AI Security team, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution. PwC Professional skills and responsibilities for this position include but are not limited to: 

  • Support the design and delivery of data risk and data classification programmes, including discovery, scoping, and rollout. 

  • Perform data discovery and sensitivity assessments across structured and unstructured data estates. 

  • Support data protection and privacy risk assessments, including DPIA inputs and data flow analysis. 

  • Contribute to the development of data handling, retention, and information protection controls. 

  • Support implementations and assessments of Microsoft Purview, including: 

  • Data discovery and classification 

  • Sensitivity labels and information protection 

  • Insider risk and data loss prevention 

  • Support clients using data security and classification platforms such as Varonis or equivalent technologies. 

  • Assist in defining operating models, governance structures, and control frameworks around data security tooling. 

  • Support AI readiness and AI risk assessments, focusing on data quality, data provenance, and access controls. 

  • Contribute to M365 Copilot readiness assessments, focusing on data exposure, oversharing risk, and control design. 

  • Support AI governance and EU AI Act readiness activities from a data and security perspective.

Purpose-led work you’ll be part of 

As a Senior Manager, you’ll be responsible for leading engagements within the Data Strategy  and Transformation service offering within PwC’s Data, Analytics & AI Consulting’s team. You’ll engage directly with clients and lead teams delivering multi-year transformation programmes.

  • Adaptable and flexible in dynamic, highly changeable environments. Able to thrive in self-directed workplaces. 

  • Experience leading and inspiring teams of technical consultants onshore, nearshore and offshore 

  • Experience mentoring junior team members and managing day-to-day activities of the team

ALG Solutions Dublin This role provides the chance to become part of an expanding ALG Solutions team, and an opportunity to create an impact in a firm that is transforming how legal professionals deliver legal services. The role sits within the eDiscovery and Investigations support team of ALG Solutions. Working with ALG Solutions teams, as well as the firm's practice groups, the Senior eDiscovery Technology Specialists will be required to provide technical and professional support to cover the full eDiscovery EDRM lifecycle and co-ordinate complex data processing and review tasks, leveraging advanced Relativity features. The role acts as a technical point of contact for troubleshooting and workflow optimisation and will support initiatives that ensure ALG remains at the forefront of digital analysis and technology-enabled eDiscovery services. As part of a forward-looking and technology-driven team, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to work at the forefront of innovation in legal services, with a particular focus on emerging technologies and Generative AI. ALG Solutions is actively exploring and implementing AI-driven solutions across eDiscovery, investigations and legal workflows, including the use of advanced analytics, machine learning and GenAI-assisted review tools. This role offers a unique opportunity to help shape how these technologies are applied in practice, contribute to the development of new solutions, and play a key role in the evolution of technology-enabled legal services. This role is a predominantly business facing role but some client facing activity is possible. This role will report to the eDiscovery Technology Manager. Duties and responsibilities Deliver high-quality client service, ensuring work is executed to agreed standards & timelines. Provide senior support on eDiscovery projects from scoping to closure, ensuring best-practice use of ALGS workflows and tools across: data collection data management processing document review production deliveries Lead the delivery of complex eDiscovery and data-related workstreams, ensuring outputs are client-ready and technically sound Engage directly with clients to understand needs, refine requirements, and propose appropriate technical and workflow solutions Proactively manage changing priorities, ensuring effective tracking, documentation and communication across stakeholders Provide guidance, knowledge-sharing and support to junior colleagues across tools, workflows, and best practices Conduct advanced troubleshooting, triage, and root-cause analysis across RelativityOne and related systems Analyse usage patterns, data behaviours, and review strategies to inform continuous improvement Review and approve user acceptance/test plans, data migration pla

ALG Solutions Dublin As a Junior Legal Applications Engineer, you will join a well-established team who are delivering innovative legal solutions using legal technology and AI for the firm and its clients. You will learn how technology is transforming legal service delivery and play a part in that journey. You will get hands-on experience working with diverse legal technology platforms, actively contribute to building and maintaining internal applications, and play an integral role in delivering legally focused, but technology-enabled projects. Collaboration is at the heart of this position: you will work side by side with legal applications experts, lawyers, IT professionals, and external suppliers to help build solutions that make a real difference to how legal services are delivered by the firm. This role provides training and mentorship from experienced team members and the opportunity to build skills in automation, workflow design, data analysis and low-code / no-code solution development. It is an excellent opportunity to begin a career in innovation and technology and join a team at the forefront of innovation in legal service delivery. This is an entry‑level position designed for candidates who have recently completed a degree in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or a related analytical field and who are seeking to begin their career in legal technology. This role reports to the Applications Development Manager. Role and responsibilities Appplication support and maintenance Assist in the basic administration, configuration and routine maintenance of legal and AI technology applications. Log issues, gather relevant information and support senior colleagues in resolving first‑level technical queries. Carry out scheduled system checks, updates and maintenance activities under supervision. Maintain accurate records of configuration changes, updates and support activity. Escalate technical or operational issues appropriately to senior team members or suppliers. Assist in creating reports and dashboards related to application usage and performance. Technical development assistance Contribute to the design and development of internal applications using a variety of technologies. Contribute to promoting the adoption of legal technology tools across the firm. Legal workflow and process support Support senior team members in developing legal workflows across all the firm’s practice areas. At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're delivering some of the world's most complex and technically advanced Life Sciences facilities. Our teams partner with leading global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to develop cutting-edge manufacturing facilities, laboratories, cleanrooms, and process plants that support the production of life-changing medicines and therapies. As our Life Sciences business continues to grow, we are seeking a Quantity Surveyor - Electrical & Instrumentation (E&I) to join our expanding team. This is an exciting opportunity to work on high-value pharmaceutical capital projects, supporting the commercial delivery of state-of-the-art facilities across Ireland and Europe.




The opportunity

As an Electrical & Instrumentation Quantity Surveyor, you will play a key role in the commercial management of major pharmaceutical and biotechnology projects from concept through construction and project closeout. You will be responsible for cost planning, estimating, contract administration, cost control, and commercial reporting for E&I packages across large-scale capital programmes. Working closely with project managers, engineers, contractors, procurement specialists, and client stakeholders, you will provide commercial expertise on electrical distribution systems, instrumentation and controls, automation infrastructure, process equipment installations, and associated utility systems within highly regulated GMP environments.




Key responsibilities

Prepare detailed quantity take-offs from engineering drawings, specifications, BIM models, and project documentation.
Develop Bills of Quantities (BoQs), cost estimates, and cost plans for Electrical & Instrumentation work packages.
Produce detailed rate analyses and cost benchmarking exercises for electrical and instrumentation systems.
Support capital cost estimating for pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities and infrastructure projects.
Monitor project budgets, forecasts, commitments, cash flow, and cost performance throughout project delivery.
Review and certify contractor applications for payment.
Evaluate variations, change orders, claims, and final accounts.
Support procurement activities, tender analysis, contract negotiations, and commercial recommendations.
Review and interpret contract clauses, specifications, drawings, and tender documentation.
Work collaboratively with Electrical, Instrumentation, Automation, Process, Mechanical, Civil, and Structural teams to support integrated project delivery.
Contribute to cost reporting, risk management, commercial governance, and project controls processes.
Utilise CostX, Bluebeam, AutoCAD, and Microsoft Excel to support estimating and commercial management activities.
Support project quality, ISO compliance, and commercial best practice initiatives.




Here's what you'll need
Degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Economics, Commercial Management, or a related discipline.
Experience in quantity surveying, commercial management, or cost management within engineering, construction, or industrial projects.
Understanding of electrical building services, power distribution systems, instrumentation, and control systems.
Experience preparing Bills of Quantities, specifications, and contract documentation.
Strong knowledge of industry-standard methods of measurement and estimating techniques.
Proficiency in CostX, Bluebeam, AutoCAD, Microsoft Excel, and related commercial software.
Ability to interpret electrical, instrumentation, control, process, civil, and architectural drawings.
Excellent commercial awareness, stakeholder management, and analytical skills.
Right to work within the EU.




Ideally, you will also have

Experience delivering pharmaceutical, biotechnology, semiconductor, or other highly regulated industrial projects.
Familiarity with GMP-regulated environments and Life Sciences project delivery.
Knowledge of building management systems (BMS), process control systems, SCADA, PLC infrastructure, and automation projects.
Experience supporting cleanroom, manufacturing, laboratory, or utility infrastructure projects.
Familiarity with FIDIC and other standard forms of contract.
Experience working in a consultancy, EPCM, or engineering design en

Business Access Manager – Ireland


Ready to take ownership of market access and make things happen?

We’re looking for a commercially sharp, proactive Business Access Manager to drive access for an innovative biosimilars portfolio across Ireland.


This is a high-impact role for someone who knows how to navigate the Irish healthcare system, build strong hospital relationships and turn commercial strategy into results. You’ll work closely with pharmacy, procurement, clinicians and payers to secure access, negotiate agreements and develop key accounts.


Covering a broad portfolio across nephrology, haematology, oncology, rheumatology and ophthalmology, this is an opportunity to work across multiple specialist therapy areas in a fast-paced, growing environment.

 

What you’ll bring

  • 3–5 years’ experience across Market Access, Key Account Management, Commercial or Pharmaceutical Sales
  • Ideally, strong biosimilars experience
  • Experience negotiating hospital commercial agreements and working with healthcare purchasing organisations
  • Strong relationships with hospital pharmacy, procurement, payers and key decision-makers
  • Experience with tenders, contract negotiations and access agreements
  • Good understanding of the Irish healthcare funding, reimbursement, pricing and market access landscape
  • Proven ability to develop account and access strategies that deliver commercial results
  • Strong commercial and analytical skills
  • Educational background in Biomedical Sciences, Health Sciences, Pharmacy, Health Economics, Business or a related discipline

 

Who we’re looking for

You’ll be a self-starter and a doer. Someone who takes ownership, moves quickly and is comfortable operating in a highly commercial environment.

You’ll be strategic but hands-on, resilient under pressure and confident building trusted relationships with senior healthcare stakeholders.

 

If you know biosimilars, understand the Irish hospital environment and enjoy turning access challenges into commercial opportunities, we’d love to hear from you.


Please note we do not sponsor Visa's for this role.

jobs.title: RWE Epidemiological Programmer – FSP (Oncology)
jobs.description_text:
IQVIA is hiring to expand our dedicated Real-World Evidence (RWE) FSP team, working fully within the environment of a prominent pharmaceutical company. This senior data analyst role sits within our Data Science, Analytics, and Technology Solutions (DATS) team and will be responsible for leading the development of datasets and conducting longitudinal analyses for observational studies in the oncology therapeutic area under a single client portfolio.
It is important that this individual has prior experience in observational research utilizing EMR and claims data, particularly in safety analyses, along with a strong statistical programming skillset and experience managing multiple studies and complex analyses. In this role, individuals will have access to real-world databases and will act as stewards of the client’s best practices, standards, and methodologies underlying the use of real-world data (RWD).
 

Essential Functions

  • Lead development of analytic datasets through raw data processing and conduct data checks / cleaning using secondary real world data sources, including claims, EHR, and lab data (must have experience in PharMetrics Plus, Flatiron, or Tempus)
  • Lead the feasibility of real-world data sources to characterize patient population, build patient cohorts, and define and validate key variables specific to study objectives.
  • Conduct and QC analyses, identification of diagnosis and treatment codes and applying statistical methods to handle censor data, confounding, and missing data.
  • Collaborate with epidemiologists to define specifications for descriptive and complex statistics (e.g., longitudinal analysis, survival analysis, regression models) in studies using RWD for oncology research questions, including safety analyses.
  • Develop and QC TFLs for protocols/reports/manuscripts using RWD (e.g. claims and EHR)
  • Support development of other study documents including protocols, statistical analysis plans, and study reports
  • Communicate timelines, progress reports, and results to project team and key stakeholders
  • Provide technical, programming, and statistical expertise and independently bring project solutions to team for complex studies

Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Data Science or related field with 5-8 years relevant experience or PhD with 3 years relevant experience
  • Strong track record of analysis of RWD using claims, EMR, and lab data (Tempus, Flatiron or PharMetrics Plus is preferred)
  • Experience analyzing oncology data and safety outcomes is preferred.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in advanced R Programming .
  • Prior pharmaceutical experience and advanced knowledge of observational research study design and analytic methodologies
  • Excellent analytic and communication skills with attention to detail
  • Ability to effectively manage and prioritize multiple tasks and projects

jobs.description_text:
Head of Sales


Europe-based | Sales Leadership | Life Sciences & Healthcare


The opportunity


IQVIA Language Solutions is building the multilingual operating layer for global life sciences—bringing together healthcare intelligence, AI-enabled workflows, specialist human expertise and the reach of IQVIA. We are moving beyond traditional translation to help customers manage critical content safely and efficiently across clinical, regulatory, safety, patient and commercial workflows.

Join a growing, entrepreneurial commercial organization and shape how IQVIA takes this next generation of language solutions to market. As Head of Sales, you will set the sales strategy, own the team quota and build a disciplined, high-performing sales organization capable of winning complex enterprise business. You will lead from the front on strategic pursuits, develop exceptional sales talent and connect IQVIA Language Solutions more deeply into the broader IQVIA portfolio and customer base.

This is a visible leadership role for a modern commercial leader who combines localization expertise, life sciences credibility and rigorous sales execution. You will have the platform to deliver meaningful growth today while building the team, operating model and executive relationships required for the future.


What you will do


  • Develop and execute the sales strategy across priority markets, customer segments, solutions and accounts, translating business goals into clear territory plans, quotas and seller-level objectives.
  • Own and exceed the team’s annual bookings, revenue and gross-margin targets, with direct accountability for new-logo acquisition, strategic account growth and predictable commercial performance.
  • Recruit, lead, coach and retain a high-performing team of enterprise sales and business development professionals; establish a culture of ambition, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Drive sales excellence through clear performance expectations, regular coaching, opportunity reviews, pipeline governance, forecasting and decisive performance management.
  • Build a healthy, qualified pipeline with the coverage and velocity required to deliver the plan; ensure CRM quality, stage integrity and reliable, evidence-based forecasts.
  • Lead pursuit strategy for the most important, complex and competitive opportunities—from executive sponsorship and value proposition through proposal, negotiation, contracting and handover.
  • Build trusted executive relationships across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, CRO and healthcare organizations, positioning IQVIA Language Solutions as a strategic multilingual content and workflow partner.
  • Partner across IQVIA to create integrated opportunities that combine Language Solutions with broader data, technology, clinical and commercial capabilities, and mobilize IQVIA account leaders around shared customer priorities.
  • Work closely with Account Management, Presales, Delivery, Technology, Quality, Marketing, Finance, Pricing and Legal to ensure that solutions are differentiated, commercially sound, operationally viable and implemented successfully.
  • Bring customer, market and competitive insight into go-to-market priorities, offering development, investment decisions and the evolution of IQVIA’s AI-enabled, human-assured language portfolio.
  • Represent IQVIA Language Solutions in executive customer engagements, industry forums and selected thought-leadership opportunities.

What success looks like


  • The sales team consistently achieves quota and delivers sustainable bookings, revenue and gross-margin growth.
  • A strong, well-qualified pipeline converts into new logos, new buying centers and larger strategic opportunities.
  • Forecasts are reliable, CRM and opportunity management are disciplined, and commercial risks are surfaced early.
  • Sellers perform at a higher level through clear expectations, active coaching, strong deal leadership and a visible talent pipeline.
  • Executive relationships deepen and integrated IQVIA pursuits create measurable customer value beyond translation fulfillment.

What you bring


  • 10+ years of progressive commercial experience, including significant leadership of enterprise sales teams across countries, regions or complex markets.
  • A proven record of building teams and consistently achieving ambitious revenue targets in language services, localization, multilingual content, life sciences technology, professional services or a closely related field.
  • Deep knowledge of the localization ecosystem and a strong understanding of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, CRO or healthcare customer needs.
  • Demonstrated ability to create and execute sales strategy, set quotas, improve seller productivity and turn pipeline discipline into predictable growth.
  • A coaching-led leadership style: you set a high bar, develop people thoughtfully, recognize performance and address gaps directly.
  • Experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise pursuits and influencing C-suite and senior functional leaders.
  • Strong commercial judgment across value-based selling, pricing, margin, proposals, negotiation, contracting and competitive positioning.
  • The ability to lead effectively in a global, matrixed organization and align diverse teams around a clear commercial outcome.
  • Curiosity about AI, localization technology and evolving content workflows, with the judgment to balance automation, human expertise, quality, security and compliance.
  • Executive presence, resilience and the communication skills to inspire a team, earn customer trust and represent a growing business internally and externally.

Why join IQVIA Language Solutions?


You will join at a pivotal point: the team is scaling its commercial organization, broadening into new life sciences workflows and building a more connected, technology-enabled portfolio. This role offers the mandate to shape the sales organization, develop outstanding commercial talent and win meaningful business with the backing of IQVIA’s global reach, healthcare expertise and customer relationships.
