jobs.description_text:
Instrument Licensing Solutions and Patient & Site Strategy helps organizations understand how patients feel and function in clinical research and routine care. The team develops and manages the instruments used to capture patient experience, oversees permissions and licensing, and guides the evolution and integration of patient- and site-facing technologies with electronic health records.


Patient Science, Instrument Development and Thought Leadership

Patient Science, Instrument R&D and Thought Leadership  develops new clinical outcome assessment instruments and expands or enhances existing instruments, with emphasis on priority therapeutic areas and market gaps. Drawing on deep expertise in instrument development, scientific consulting, and delivery, the team supports client engagements in collaboration with Patient and Clinical Technology (PACT), IQVIA Laboratories, digital-measure scientists, imaging-measurement scientists, COA managers and therapeutic-area centers of excellence. The team also advances thought leadership through white papers, peer-reviewed publications, books, posters, and podium presentations, working closely with clients, regulators, patient advocacy organizations, industry experts, and other stakeholders.


Position

Composite and companion measures represent an important advance in measuring what matters to patients. By integrating multiple sources of evidence, they help move health care and clinical research beyond measures of service utilization toward a more complete understanding of meaningful outcomes.

This role leads the strategic, scientific, and regulatory development of laboratory- and genomic-enabled composite and companion measures in partnership with IQVIA Labs and external partners. These solutions are designed for use by biopharmaceutical and medical-device organizations in clinical trials and real-world studies, as well as by health care professionals in routine clinical practice.

The Senior Director ensures that the patient perspective is rigorously measured and incorporated into drug-development strategy, laboratory and genomic research, clinical outcome assessment endpoint strategy, regulatory submissions, and commercialization through the application of behavioral and measurement science.


Role Overview

The Senior Director Composite Measures Science & Integration leads the design, development, validation, and implementation of scientifically rigorous composite and companion measurement solutions in partnership with IQVIA Labs and external partners. The role supports corporate strategy, client requirements, global clinical trials, real-world research, and patient-facing care by integrating clinical outcome assessments, digital measures, laboratory and genomic data, and emerging technologies into meaningful endpoints and scalable service offerings aligned with market needs and the IQVIA solutions portfolio.


Strategic and Scientific Leadership

Set the strategy, scientific direction, and operating model for Laboratory & Genomic composite and companion measure development.

Partner with IQVIA Labs scientific team and external partners on scientific evolution and market needs.

Assess the feasibility and value of applying measurement science, laboratory methods, digital technologies, and novel data sources to products and services.

Align measurement research and development priorities with corporate strategy, business objectives, client needs, regulatory expectations, and market dynamics.

Maintain expert knowledge of developments in drug development, clinical outcome assessment, digital health technology, laboratory science, genomics, patient care, and relevant regulatory guidance.

Serve as a recognized internal and external scientific authority and as the primary technical contact for complex, cross-functional contracts and projects.


Core Responsibilities

  • Direct the end-to-end development, validation, integration, and delivery of composite measures that combine laboratory, genomic and other clinically relevant data with patient-reported, clinician-reported and digital outcome data.
  • Ensure that COA data collection, digital-measure data, laboratory operations, and associated deliverables meet applicable scientific, quality, privacy, and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead research design and execution, including validation protocols, analytical methods, technical reports, troubleshooting strategies, and short- and long-term project goals.
  • Oversee the evaluation and validation of relevant laboratory measurement instruments and methods, including installation, operational, and performance qualification documentation, as appropriate in collaboration with IQVIA Labs and external partners.
  • Ensure the high-quality, timely delivery of clinical research and health care solutions while maintaining exceptional standards of client service.
  • Use performance indicators, process analysis and AI to improve efficiency, scalability, cost control, resource utilization, and readiness for growth.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives and collaborate with therapeutic-area experts, consulting teams, regulators, clients, patient advocacy organizations, industry thought leaders, technology partners, and other stakeholders.

Innovation, Publications, and Partnerships

  • Translate scientific and technological advances into differentiated service offerings for clinical research and patient-facing care.
  • Advance scientific literature and industry dialogue through peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstracts, posters, podium presentations, white papers, books, patent applications, and scientifically accurate marketing materials.
  • Lead or support the development of intellectual property, vendor agreements, research collaborations, and strategic partnerships.
  • Identify proactive client solutions that create scientific value, strengthen market differentiation, and support sustainable revenue growth.

People and Operational Leadership

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary team through effective recruitment, onboarding, training, mentorship, performance management, and succession planning.
  • Foster a unified culture of collaboration, information sharing, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish and manage operating budgets, resource plans, cost-control standards, and capacity strategies.
  • Partner with Quality Assurance and operational teams to implement effective quality programs, address performance issues promptly, and maintain current procedures and staff capabilities.
  • Manage staff in accordance with organizational policies and applicable regulations, including work planning, assignment, professional development, employee relations, and appropriate human-resources actions.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
  • At least 15 years of relevant experience, including substantial experience in scientific method development, clinical laboratory or drug-development solutions, and people leadership.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of scientific principles, measurement theory, method development, drug development, and relevant state-of-the-art instrumentation and technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence across organizational boundaries, lead multiple workstreams, manage complex projects, and communicate effectively with clients and senior leaders.
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal, analytical, presentation, and client-management capabilities, with the ability to translate scientific insight into practical, scalable, and commercially relevant solutions.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and ensure that they are performed in a quality manner.
  • Strong knowledge of the BioPharma drug development industry and applying that knowledge to the improvement of their business unit.
  • Effective communication and presentation skills to influence at various levels of the business, including senior leadership.
  • Skill in extracting relevant data to measure performance indicators and proactively plan for growth and scalability.

jobs.description_text:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

11

The Team:

S&P Global Ratings' Corporates practice assesses the creditworthiness of companies across industries by analyzing business risk, strategy, competitive position, and financial performance to support transparent and comparable decision-making. The European Telecommunications, Media, Technology and Entertainment team comprises analysts based across London, Paris, Frankfurt, Stockholm, and Madrid, covering a portfolio of investment-grade and speculative-grade corporate entities. This breadth offers analysts a distinctive opportunity to build deep credit expertise across some of Europe's most dynamic and fast-evolving sectors.

Responsibilities and Impact:

Team Contribution & Capability Building
•    Guide and coach junior analysts and research staff, building capability in credit analysis, data discipline, and analytical tooling to reinforce consistent, high-quality outputs.
•    Strengthen team productivity by creating reusable analytical assets and contributing to automation initiatives that free capacity for human analysis and judgment.
•    Identify and propose workflow improvements that remove unnecessary manual steps without compromising governance or analytical standards.

Core Analytical & Delivery
•    Lead end-to-end credit analysis and surveillance for assigned corporate credits, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery with clear accountability for outputs and priorities.
•    Synthesize portfolio performance, market signals, and peer context into decision-ready insights that support rating committee discussions and risk assessments.
•    Embed and validate generative AI and large language model tools within analytical workflows, maintaining human accountability for all conclusions and material risk judgments.

Stakeholder & Market Engagement
•    Engage with issuer management teams and external stakeholders alongside senior team members, translating complex analysis into clear, evidence-based narratives for clients and rating committees.
•    Prepare well-structured committee materials and act as a spokesperson for S&P Global Ratings when required.

Risk Management and Operating
•    Apply methodology, confidentiality, and data governance requirements consistently, escalating issues early with clear recommendations to protect analytical integrity.
•    Contribute to the responsible design and testing of automation and AI-enabled workflows, maintaining clear boundaries between what can be automated and what requires human judgment.

What We're Looking For:

Required Skills and Experience:
•    An S&P Global employee at this level would typically have 3 to 5 years of relevant work experience in credit analysis.
•    Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality work across multiple credits with limited oversight, and to coach junior colleagues through shared analytical standards and tools.
•    Strong collaboration and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence through credibility and constructive engagement.
•    Demonstrated credit, financial, and risk analysis skills, with the ability to link fundamental business and sector drivers to forward-looking risk views.
•    Practical experience embedding generative AI or large language model tools into professional workflows to improve productivity and analytical output.
•    Proficiency in analytical and spreadsheet tools, with a willingness to develop skills in data and automation platforms.
•    Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex analytical content into clear, concise narratives for senior stakeholders and rating committees.
•    High standards for analytical quality, traceability, and governance, with sound judgment on the responsible use of AI tools in a controlled environment.
•    Demonstrated ability to contribute to automation workflow design and testing, with clear judgment on which analytical decisions require human oversight.

Preferred or Helpful Experience:
•    Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent preferred. A master’s degree or professional certification (such as CFA) is highly valued. We welcome candidates from traditional finance disciplines as well as diverse academic backgrounds that support innovative and critical thinking.
•    Direct experience analyzing corporate entities in Telecommunications, Media, Technology, or Entertainment sectors.

Additional Information:
•    Employees are required to work from the office a minimum of two days per week.
•    Candidates who reach the final stage of the interview process will be asked to attend at least one in-person interview at their nearest S&P Global Ratings office before an offer can be extended. 


 

About S&P Global Ratings
At S&P Global Ratings, our analyst-driven credit ratings, research, and sustainable finance opinions provide critical insights that are essential to translating complexity into clarity so market participants can uncover opportunities and make decisions with conviction. By bringing transparency to the market through high-quality independent opinions on creditworthiness, we enable growth across a wide variety of organizations, including businesses, governments, and institutions.

S&P Global Ratings is a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI).  S&P Global is the world’s foremost provider of credit ratings, benchmarks, analytics and workflow solutions in the global capital, commodity and automotive markets. With every one of our offerings, we help many of the world’s leading organizations navigate the economic landscape so they can plan for tomorrow, today.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management
jobs.description_text:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

12

The Team: The Data Privacy, Protection and Governance team at S&P Global is dedicated to managing sensitive, personal, and non-personal information. We achieve this through the implementation of comprehensive policies, processes, controls, and metrics that ensure compliance with global regulations.

 

The Impact: S&P Global is seeking an

Director, Information Governance and Records Management to lead, mature, and scale the enterprise-wide information governance and records management program across its global data and analytics business, with supporting responsibility for data governance, privacy by design, and AI governance.

 

This role owns the strategy, policies, standards, and controls that govern the full lifecycle of S&P Global’s business records and information, from creation and capture through classification, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition. The Director will ensure that records and information management practices align with S&P Global’s Information Governance Policy framework, Privacy Program, and evolving legal, regulatory, and recordkeeping obligations across jurisdictions.

 

The position plays a critical leadership role in operationalizing the enterprise records retention schedule, strengthening information classification compliance, and reducing over-retention risk, while supporting a risk-based data management and governance model, privacy by design, and responsible AI practices that underpin S&P Global’s delivery of data-driven products and services, including analytics, ratings, market intelligence, and entity-based data solutions.

 

S&P Global’s business model—focused on delivering data, analytics, and insight to global markets—requires robust governance over data sourcing, processing, retention, and usage to ensure trust, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience.

 

What’s in it for you: In this role, you will:

  • Collaborate with senior and executive stakeholders globally.
  • Act as a senior advisor to stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business divisions.
  • Lead cross-functional governance forums to drive alignment and accountability for data governance activities.
  • Be an integral part of building and maturing the global Information Governance and Records Management program, working alongside executive leadership to drive our team forward.

Responsibilities: The Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management will be responsible for:

 

  • Information Governance & Records Management Leadership
    • Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Information Governance and Records Management program, covering the full information lifecycle (creation, capture, use, storage, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition) across paper and electronic records.
    • Own and maintain core policies and standards, including:
      • Information Governance Policy
      • Information Classification Standard
      • Records Retention Schedule
      • Legal Hold and Defensible Disposition procedures
    • Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, internal risk frameworks, and international standards.
    • Maintain and periodically refresh the global Records Retention Schedule, conducting legal and regulatory retention research across jurisdictions and securing business sign-off on record classes and retention periods.
    • Drive operational adoption of retention requirements across business divisions and enterprise systems, including records inventories, system-level retention configuration, and coordinated defensible disposition of records and data that have met their retention periods.
    • Partner with Legal and eDiscovery teams to manage the legal hold process and ensure holds override routine disposition.
    • Develop and deliver information governance and records management training, communications, and a network of divisional records coordinators.

 

  • Data Classification & Information Handling
    • Establish and oversee enterprise-wide data classification frameworks and compliance monitoring.
    • Partner with Information Security and technology teams to ensure appropriate controls for data access, storage, and protection.
    • Implement and track metrics to measure classification compliance and data handling effectiveness.

 

  • Data Management & Governance
    • Support the development of a scalable, enterprise data management and governance model that integrates with records and retention requirements, including:
      • Data inventory and cataloging
      • Data ownership and stewardship
      • Data flow visibility and control
    • Collaborate with business, technology, and risk teams to ensure governance controls are embedded across products, platforms, and operations.

  • Risk Management & Regulatory Readiness
    • Identify, assess, and mitigate risks relating to data governance, retention, classification, and regulatory compliance.
    • Support internal audits, regulatory inquiries, and external assessments.
    • Maintain audit-ready documentation and evidence of compliance.

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Oversight
    • Act as Information Governance and Data Compliance support for the development, implementation, and continuous enhancement of S&P Global’s AI governance framework, ensuring the responsible, ethical, and compliant use of artificial intelligence and automated decision-making technologies across the enterprise, including appropriate classification, retention, and disposition of AI training data, inputs, and outputs.
    • Where necessary, establish and oversee policies, standards, controls, and risk assessment processes governing the lifecycle of AI systems, including model development, procurement, deployment, monitoring, and retirement.
    • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Information Security, Technology, Risk, and business stakeholders to ensure AI initiatives align with regulatory requirements, corporate policies, data governance standards, and responsible AI principles, while promoting transparency, accountability, and effective risk management.

Lead the space management and co-ordination for projects, including equipment stack-up studies, pipe rack & services design, room layout etc. Support development of each discipline Design Philosophy. Carry out design risk assessment. Input into development of the Integrated Project S Develop and manage the discipline estimates and resource loading for DeLPD administration support. Coordinate 3rd Party Designers e. Cleanroom, Sprinklers, Super skids etc. Chair weekly internal model design co-ordination meeting to review model progress and/or issues effecting modelling ef Manage and interface with 3D design leads. Regular face-to-face, phone and Teams communication with all the disciplines ensuring coordination plays a key role in daily activities. Manage the co-ordination of all design disciplines in the model and their space allocations (both internal and external). Identify and resolve any design coordination issues. Management of early discipline release in an area before other disciplines progressed significantly or complete. Expedite weekly vendor information that modellers need to complete. Monitor information flow. Coordinate design reviews - both formal (with client) and informal (internal). Manage closeout of action items during design reviews and clash reports. Expedite clash resolution. Coordinate commencement and completion of checking activities. Manage Overall Model Progress Reporting & MTOs. Manage the deliverable issue schedule versus the construction schedule Manage changes to scope & requirements and identify changes to disciplines and the Project Manager. Production of Discipline Deliverable Prioritise procurement of items that have largest impact on modelling. Perform work in compliance with PM Group’s Quality Management System Qualifications Batchelor’s Degree in an Engineering or Architectural discipline is strongly preferred. Ideally 10+ Years of design experience in a design firm setting (preferably in the Pharmaceutical, Biopharmaceutical, Cell & Gene Therapy sectors). An understanding of all Disciplines and their 3D applications. The candidate must have a complete understanding of technical principles, theories and the concepts of spatial design of complex process facilities including but not limited to process piping design. Knowledge of international and local standards with regards safe operation and maintenance impacting building layout design. Commercially aware with the ability to undertake value engineering activities and implement new technologies to provide cost effective solutions for our clients. Commercially aware on project execution, control of budgets, resourcing and change control. Multiple office execution experience advantageous. Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to prepare written specifications and contract documents is required. Professional approach and demeanour with a strong ethical approach to safety, quality, environmental protection and business. Ability to play a positive role in multi-discipline teams with a reliable, consistent and mature approach to work. Inclusion and Diversity are core to our culture and values. Wherever we work, we commit to a culture of mutual respect and belonging by building a truly inclusive workplace rich in diverse people, talents and ideas. Valuing the contributions of all our people and respecting individual differences will sustain our growth into the future. PM Group is committed to ensuring our hiring process is fair and accessible to all and will provide candidates with disabilities with reasonable accommodations required to participate in the recruitment process. If you require any assistance in this regard, please let us know.

Role Purpose: We are seeking a motivated Front End Engineer to join our team in Dublin, building and maintaining our customer facing web applications, used by millions of customers across Ireland. Overview


Susquehanna's technology organisation is growing fast, and engineering hiring has become a critical enabler of the firm’s technology and business priorities. To support this growth, we are creating a new role within our EMEA Recruitment team. We are looking for an experienced Technology Recruitment Lead to lead and develop the team and strengthen technology recruitment across the region.

This new position will provide you with the opportunity to be part of an innovative, fast-paced, and high-performing regional recruitment function in a highly collaborative global organisation.

You will lead the EMEA Technology recruitment team, set its recruitment and sourcing strategy, in line with our business priorities, partner directly with senior technology stakeholders across the business, and collaborate with recruiting leads in our Philadelphia, Hong Kong, and Sydney offices. You will also personally manage selected priority searches, playing a key role in the continued delivery of world-class technology talent to Susquehanna.

The Role

 

This is a hands-on leadership role. The key responsibilities of this role include:

Development and implementation of the EMEA technology recruitment strategy, aligning with business priorities and clear objectives across stakeholder management, pipeline quality, candidate experience, and delivery.
Leadership and development of the team. Coach, mentor, support and advise each recruiter to build their capability, set clear goals, and hold regular performance conversations, building capability and accountability across the team.
Set clear expectations across the team for a well-managed recruitment process.
Own the delivery of end-to-end selected technology recruitment processes, from sourcing and interviewing through to offer management.
Implement a solution-driven approach to the delivery of the EMEA technology workforce plan along with the relevant HR and Business partners.
Use recruitment data to assess pipeline health, identify bottlenecks and guide decisions on sourcing, selection, and offer strategy. Translate insights into clear actions that improve hiring outcomes and candidate experience with continuous measurement of this impact.
Partner with our Marketing team to shape our employer branding strategy for the region.
Lead the presence of Susquehanna at relevant industry events and play a key role in strengthening our engagement with future top technology talent for Susquehanna.
Build out the sourcing strategy and enable the team to bring it to life, using market insights to identify and engage future talent and build high-quality talent pipelines aligned to Susquehanna's needs and strategy.
Partner with and advise our EMEA technology leaders, using market data and talent insight to inform hiring priorities, advise on talent availability and agree effective approaches to attracting the best skills relevant to their teams’ requirements.
Collaborate with recruitment leads cross-regionally to drive consistency and alignment in the development and implementation of our recruitment strategy.
Own the candidate experience. Susquehanna is a collaborative, personable, and grounded organisation, and we aim to give every candidate an exceptional recruitment process.
Oversee the team's continued delivery of a highly effective and efficient candidate experience throughout the recruitment lifecycle, making sure candidates receive consistent communication and timely feedback in line with agreed service standards.

What we're looking for

You will have at least 7 years' experience within a regional/global recruitment function with a strong track record in technology recruitment.
You must have In-house recruiting experience and at least three years' experience directly managing, coaching, and developing a high-performing recruitment team, with demonstrated ability to build team capability and improve performance.
You will demonstrate your success as a recruitment expert, including direct end-to-end recruitment across a range of technology roles including software engineers, developers and technicians. Overseeing the full recruitment process from sourcing, interviewing, offer management and candidate relationship management.
Be results driven, with a true demonstration in the delivery of exceptional talent, candidate experience and stakeholder management within a fast-paced technology environment.
Experience leading a recruitment team in technology, finance, or fintech is strongly preferred; candidates from other fast-paced, high-volume environments will be considered.

Deliver planned improvement projects, with time allocated to complete them, and contribute to configuration, capacity and resilience improvements alongside infrastructure teams.

Overview


 

We are seeking an experienced Technology Risk and Controls Analyst to join Susquehanna's Dublin Technology Risk team.

Working with technology and business teams, you will help identify and assess risks, strengthen controls and deliver practical improvements. You will contribute across a varied portfolio of reviews, projects and ongoing activities, adapting as priorities and business needs evolve.

We are looking for someone who is curious, practical and comfortable tackling unfamiliar problems. You should enjoy learning how things work, making sense of incomplete information and working with others to find solutions. Strong judgement, clear communication and the ability to take ownership and follow through are central to the role.

You will work closely with experienced technology teams in a trading environment, take ownership of meaningful risk work and have the opportunity to improve how the team operates. The variety of assignments will allow you to apply your existing strengths and broaden your experience.

What You Will Do
Assess technology risks. Review applications, infrastructure and operational processes to understand potential business impacts, evaluate existing safeguards and recommend proportionate improvements. Contribute to risk and control self-assessments and keep assigned risk records current.
Review controls and evidence. Assess control design and evidence of operation, identify gaps and document clear findings. Carry out assigned technology and trading application reviews, support audit requests and work with owners to improve evidence quality.
Drive remediation and reporting. Agree actions, owners and target dates with technical teams, assess completion evidence and escalate material issues. Prepare accurate risk reports and key risk indicators that explain progress, emerging concerns and decisions required.
Support resilience and lifecycle improvements. Contribute to business continuity exercises, application load and resilience testing, incident follow-up and technology lifecycle reviews. Use findings and operational data to identify dependencies, unsupported technology and other exposures, then track agreed improvements.
Improve processes and tools. Help refine risk workflows, dashboards and evidence collection. Define requirements, test changes and use data analysis, automation and AI tools to reduce repetitive work while validating the results.
Contribute across the team's priorities. Support policy and procedure reviews, risk awareness activities and assessments of emerging technologies. Work with colleagues and specialists on new assignments, applying sound judgement as requirements evolve.

You will manage an agreed portfolio within the first line, working with control owners and partnering with second-line Risk, Compliance and Audit. 


What we're looking for

What We Are Looking For
Typically 4–7 years of relevant experience in technology risk, technology controls, IT audit, operational resilience, or a technical role with substantial risk and control responsibilities. Equivalent experience and demonstrated capability will be considered.
Experience delivering risk assessments or control reviews, producing clear findings and following remediation through to completion.
Practical understanding of applications and infrastructure, including change management, access controls, monitoring, recovery, capacity and technology lifecycle risks.
Ability to assess whether evidence demonstrates that a control works, identify missing information and explain the significance of a gap.
Confidence working with AI,reports/.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn technical information into concise assessments, management updates and actionable recommendations.
Confidence working with experienced technical colleagues, asking constructive questions and agreeing practical next steps.
Good organisation, adaptability and judgement, with the ability to manage several assignments, learn unfamiliar subjects and recognise when to escalate.
A relevant degree or equivalent professional experience.

Excellent attention to detail

jobs.description_text: Emerge, thrive and lead in a dynamic and collaborative environment at DCU. With over 20,000 students in five faculties across three campuses, we excel in research, innovation, engagement and opportunity. DCU is committed to the values of equality, diversity and inclusion as reflected in a broad range of institutional initiatives addressing gender under-representation, socioeconomic disadvantage and disability. Join us in our mission to transform lives and societies. Why work at DCU?

jobs.title: When will I know about the interview?
jobs.description_text: When will I know about the interview? We aim to give candidates two weeks' notice for interviews. How do I prepare for a DCU interview? Review the job description, research DCU and the Faculty, Unit or Research Centre you’re applying to. Think of examples based on the assessment criteria in the job description and reflect on your experience and how it aligns. Can I get accommodations for my interview? Yes, DCU is committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employment. Please don’t hesitate to contact the recruitment team for accommodations. Do I need to make a presentation at my interview? You'll be told if a presentation is required. Candidates should send a copy of their presentation to the recruitment team at an agreed date in advance of their interview. What is DCU’s interview format? The interview panel typically includes four members: the hiring manager, an internal expert, an external expert, and a DCU People team member. Sometimes, there may be up to six panel members. Before the interview, candidates will receive the names of the panel members. During the interview, you'll discuss your previous experience, education, and training. You'll also answer questions based on the job description's assessment criteria. At the end, you can ask the panel about the role, department, unit, or DCU. When are referees contacted? After the interview, DCU will contact your references. Once the references have been returned, you will be informed whether or not you have been deemed appointable. For some roles, DCU may contact referees in advance of the interview. When will I know the interview outcome? We endeavour to ensure you’re updated within 10 working days of the interview. Can I get feedback on my interview? Yes. The hiring manager will be able to provide unsuccessful candidates with feedback upon request.

The Associate will help oversee fund accounting, Net Asset Value (NAV), financial reporting, controls, and service-provider delivery while partnering across Investments, Valuations, Product, Finance, and Operations. About the Firm At BlackRock, our mission is to help more people experience financial well-being. Our investment, technology, and operating capabilities enable us to serve clients across public and private markets. This opportunity provides exposure to BlackRock’s alternatives platform while contributing to the accurate, controlled, and scalable financial oversight that supports our clients and investment businesses. Team Overview Alternatives Fund Controllers supports BlackRock’s alternatives business through accounting and financial oversight of complex investment funds. The team partners with investment teams, Product Strategy, Valuations, external fund administrators, auditors, and other internal stakeholders to support accurate and timely fund reporting. Coverage may include private equity, real estate, infrastructure, private credit, hedge funds, and fund-of-funds structures. Role Overview The Associate will take ownership of day-to-day accounting and administrator oversight for assigned alternative investment funds. The role combines detailed financial review with risk management, stakeholder coordination, and continuous improvement. Success requires an ability to understand complex fund structures, identify and resolve accounting or reporting issues, maintain a strong control environment, and deliver high-quality outcomes across recurring and project-based responsibilities. Key Responsibilities You will: Review NAV and accounting packages prepared by external fund administrators, analyzing profit and loss, balance-sheet movements, investor allocations, and other material activity. Validate management fees, performance fees, carried interest, and other fund calculations in accordance with governing documents and applicable accounting requirements. Oversee administrator and service-provider delivery, helping ensure financial and investor reporting is accurate, timely, and supported by a robust control environment. Support fund lifecycle events including launches, capital calls, distributions, administrator onboarding, and liquidations. Review financial reporting and support annual audits, regulatory reporting, and responses to auditor and stakeholder requests. Partner with Investments, Valuations, Product, Finance, Operations, auditors, and external administrators to resolve accounting and operational issues. Identify and escalate valuation, accounting, operational, or control risks and contribute to effective remediation. Analyze complex fund activity and governing documents to support accurate accounting treatment and reporting. Drive improvements in processes, controls, automation, data quality, and scalability across fund-controller workflows. Contribute to a collaborative, accountable team culture while developing deeper expertise across alternative investments and fund structures. Required Qualifications You have: 4+ years in fund accounting, investment accounting, audit, fund operations, asset management, or a related financial-services discipline, consistent with BlackRock’s Associate-level framework. A bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field. Strong accounting and financial-analysis capabilities, including experience interpreting financial statements and investigating accounting or reporting issues. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills. A strong risk and control mindset with the judgment to identify issues and escalate appropriately. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams and third-party service providers. Technology & Digital Fluency: Ability to use technology, data, automation, analytics, and AI-enabled tools to improve productivity, strengthen decision-making, reduce risk, and enhance processes. The salary range for Ireland is 75000 - 105000 EUR Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance. Our benefits To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. Our hybrid work model BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock. Water & Wastewater Account Manager

Siemens Digital Industries

Location: Ireland

 

Help shape the future of Ireland's water and wastewater industry

Siemens Digital Industries is seeking a commercially minded Water & Wastewater Account Manager to drive growth across one of our largest and fastest-growing market sectors in Ireland.

This is an external, customer-facing sales role focused on developing new business opportunities, growing existing accounts and increasing Siemens' market presence within the Water & Wastewater sector.

This is an exciting opportunity to take ownership of a strategically important market, working closely with Ireland's main government water organisation and key industry stakeholders to promote Siemens' leading automation, digitalisation and electrification solutions.

The Water & Wastewater sector is one of Siemens Digital Industries' largest and fastest-growing market segments in Ireland, supported by significant long-term infrastructure investment and an established customer base. This role offers the opportunity to shape future growth across a strategically important sector while helping deliver critical infrastructure for communities across Ireland.

 

The Role

As the dedicated Account Manager for the Water & Wastewater sector, you will lead Siemens' commercial growth strategy across Ireland. Working alongside end users, consultants, system integrators, OEMs and engineering contractors, you'll identify new projects, influence specifications and position Siemens as a preferred technology partner.

Success in this role will come from expanding existing accounts, developing new business and supporting customers in delivering critical water and wastewater infrastructure projects.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and grow strategic relationships with key water and wastewater customers, particularly Ireland's main government water organisation.
Drive sustainable business growth by identifying opportunities where Siemens solutions can add value and increase market presence within the sector.
Develop and execute a commercial strategy for the Water & Wastewater market across Ireland.
Promote Siemens' automation, digitalisation, electrification and related technology solutions.
Engage with consultants, system integrators, OEMs, engineering contractors and partners to influence specifications and identify opportunities.
Develop and strengthen relationships across the wider water and wastewater ecosystem.
Identify, develop and convert new business opportunities across water treatment, wastewater treatment and associated infrastructure projects.
Work collaboratively with Siemens' technical and commercial teams to deliver customer-focused solutions.
 

About You

Essential

Proven experience in external sales, business development or commercial account management with responsibility for revenue growth.
Experience selling engineering, automation, electrical, instrumentation or industrial technology solutions into utilities, infrastructure or industrial customers.
Experience managing a sales territory, achieving revenue targets and developing new business opportunities.
Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to engage with customers, consultants and technical decision-makers.
Proven ability to identify, develop and convert new business opportunities while growing existing customer relationships.
A proactive and commercially focused approach, with a passion for building long-term customer partnerships and delivering growth.

Desirable

Experience within the water and wastewater sector would be advantageous. We also welcome applications from candidates with experience in industrial automation, process industries, electrical infrastructure, utilities, manufacturing or other engineering-led sales environments.
Experience working with consultants, system integrators, OEMs, contractors or channel partners would also be beneficial.
 

We'd particularly welcome applications from candidates working in business development, technical sales, account management or sales leadership roles within industrial automation, utilities, infrastructure, process industries or related engineering sectors.

We know that not every candidate will meet every requirement. If you have a track record of developing customer relationships and selling technical or engineering-led solutions, we'd encourage you to apply.

AWS has successfully launched the European Sovereign Cloud (ESC), marking a significant development in Utility Computing (UC). To spearhead this initiative, we are actively seeking experienced systems engineers with a strong background in cloud operations. As part of the AWS Managed Operations team, you will play a pivotal role in building, operating and evolving operations and development teams dedicated to delivering high-availability AWS services, including EC2, S3, Dynamo, Lambda, and Bedrock, exclusively for EU customers. For more information on ESC please check out our blog: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/in-the-works-aws-european-sovereign-cloud/

Your responsibilities will encompass overseeing the ongoing operations and expansion of the ESC, working closely with global AWS teams, and influencing the evolution of AWS services and technology. A typical day in this role involves collaborating with technology leaders, contributing to the enhancement of day-to-day operations, and ensuring continuous improvements in availability, reliability, latency, performance, and efficiency of the ESC.

The overarching goal is to deliver scalable services and ensure a high-availability experience for EU customers. If you are an experienced professional ready for a challenging and impactful opportunity, we invite you to join our efforts in operating and scaling a best-in-class development engineering and operations team that aligns with AWS' commitment to customer satisfaction and continual innovation.

Utility Computing (UC)
European Sovereign Cloud (ESC) is a part of AWS Utility Computing (UC).
AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS. Within AWS UC, Managed Operations engineers engage with AWS customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.

Eligibility requirement
- Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
- Candidate must be a national of an EU member state and residing in the EU to operate the AWS European Sovereign Cloud.
- Amazon will provide relocation support for successful applicants relocating within the European Union.
- Employees will participate in an On-Call rota.

Embark on a week filled with meaningful contributions to the operation and improvement of significant software systems. You dedicate a substantial portion of your time to carefully review the operational health of services within your team's responsibility. In the process, you diligently identify anomalies and craft actionable bug reports, aspiring to enhance the overall efficiency and performance of your systems.

In addition to these responsibilities, you offer constructive feedback on change management documents and work earnestly to address your team's operational backlog. Through a collaborative effort, you strive to navigate challenges and ensure the seamless functionality of your systems. Additionally, you engage in the development and testing of scripts, hoping to provide practical solutions to enhance your workflows.

Beyond the technical aspects, you assume a role as an educator, sharing insights on the complexities of the European Sovereign Cloud with service teams. It's a humbling experience for you to contribute to the collective knowledge of the team, fostering a culture of mutual understanding.

This week encapsulates your commitment to continuous learning and improvement, acknowledging that every effort, no matter how small, contributes to the collective success of your team and the reliability of your software systems.

In addition to these responsibilities, your position involves 24x7 on-call responsibility. You work as a team to root-cause issues and ensure your systems remain resilient and fault-tolerant, underscoring your commitment to maintaining operational excellence.

The ideal candidate possesses a strong work ethic, attention to detail, the ability to meet deadlines, and a commitment to Safety & Operational Excellence.



Key job responsibilities
Logistics Specialists monitor inventory levels to ensure that proper stock levels are maintained to support build and repair activities. They receive parts, maintain inventory, and check-out parts as needed to Data Center Technicians and Engineers. They will also be responsible for loading and unloading shipments and transporting parts between different locations. This position involves frequent lifting of materials and products. Logistics Specialists will be required to keep precise records of all commodities going in and out of company. They also maintain the cleanliness, organization, and safety of all workspaces. They must be available to work shift work.


About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Diverse Experiences

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer, Amazon Foundational Security Services
jobs.description_text:
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Our team is looking for a highly motivated Systems Engineer in Amazon Security who will raise the security bar by delivering industry-best security services. You should be somebody who enjoys inventing and simplifying around complex security challenges, obsesses over the customer experience, and feels strongly about delivering results. You should be passionate about solving security hurdles in innovative ways. We do not desire to simply produce good software here at Amazon Security... we want to produce disruptive, industry-leading innovations.

The EUSC Operations team runs a 24/7/365 operation, and on-call support will be required as part of this role. You would join the on-call rotation approximately once every 4–6 weeks.
Our team values work-life harmony. Being part of a 24/7/365 on-call rotation is an important aspect of maintaining operational excellence in this role, and we understand that striking a healthy balance between your personal and professional life is crucial to your happiness and success here. On-call rotations are structured to be manageable — occurring roughly once every 4–6 weeks — so that you can stay engaged and effective without feeling overburdened. We encourage members of the team to use personal time as needed to cultivate this balance and to promote a productive and well-balanced life — both in and outside of work.

Key job responsibilities
Each day, hundreds of thousands of developers and customers make billions of transactions worldwide on our cloud and the Amazon retail site. jobs.title: T&S Specialist I, AWS Trust & Safety
jobs.description_text:
The T&S Specialist I is a specialist role in AWS Trust & Safety covering customer account investigations, service-related case resolution, and abuse mitigation across AWS infrastructure and services. You will investigate customer problems with their Amazon services accounts — for cases that may be more time-sensitive and where SOPs or technical documentation may not be well-defined. You will act as a developing subject matter expert (SME) in your domain area, identifying root causes, flagging known risks, and providing escalation support to peers and cross-functional partners.

You will collaborate across T&S and with internal stakeholders (Policy, Legal, Product and Engineering Teams) to drive high-quality business support for AWS customers. The role is both operational and strategic. Operationally, you will dive into technical details to diagnose issues, determine resolution for high-impact scenarios, guide customers toward self-service resources, and escalate appropriately when issues are large, critical, or complex. Strategically, you will identify opportunities and risks with customers' technical decisions that may have financial or data security impact, contribute to knowledge base improvements, and help shape more effective SOPs and customer-facing documentation.

A defining feature of this role is its relationship to continuous improvement. You will not only resolve cases — you will work with your team and management to improve how customer issues are identified, documented, and resolved, using case outcomes and process insights to drive efficiency over time. You will also contribute to team development by helping train new peers, participating in the interview process, and submitting suggestions that make knowledge base articles and user documentation more effective. As a technically proficient member of the team with 2+ years of experience and working knowledge across security, account management, and Amazon services, you will also act in a mentoring capacity whenever possible, helping ensure the continued growth and success of the AWS Trust & Safety team.

Key job responsibilities
- Become a subject matter expert (SME) across complex, legally sensitive abuse types — including child safety and exploitation, image-based sexual abuse, terrorist and violent extremist content, AI-generated content and all types of abuse outlined in the AWS Acceptable Use Policy — spanning multiple AWS services, providing guidance, escalation support, and deep-dive analysis for internal and external stakeholders.

- Assess and own escalated AWS customer issues in order to provide accurate support. Act as a high-judgement decision maker for escalated situations where there may be no established SOP.

- Act as the Voice of the Customer by reporting and acting on observed areas for improvement while actively seeking solutions to customer needs, communicating trends to leadership, and suggesting innovative solutions on behalf of the customer experience.

- Drive projects that improve support-related functions and processes. Define project goals and objectives with cross-functional teams; create detailed project plans (timelines, milestones, resource allocation); and manage timelines to ensure on-time delivery.

- Assume responsibility for developing detailed knowledge about AWS specific services and then using that knowledge to identify gaps.

- Be a team player with the ability to work in large groups and independently

- Due to the 24x7 operations of the business, must be able to work a flexible work schedule that may include nights, weekends, holidays, overtime, etc.

About the team
You'll be joining the AWS Trust & Safety (T&S) Team, a global unit dedicated to protecting AWS services from abuse while maintaining customer trust. The team acts as the first line of defense for AWS, analyzing trends and reporting findings to service teams. Your role will involve working closely with various stakeholders — including Policy, Legal, and AWS Account teams — to develop scalable and sustainable solutions that protect against and mitigate abuse. The T&S team is crucial to ensuring that Amazon Web Services remains the most customer-centric company on Earth.

jobs.description_text:
We're part of the AWS Observability organization. We build the tools customers use to understand how their applications and infrastructure are performing, and to fix problems fast. Our data platform collects operational signals — metrics, logs, and traces — from systems running at enormous scale, and turns them into the analytics, dashboards, and insights customers act on. We run this for Amazon itself and for millions of customers worldwide.

Two things shape our roadmap. We build on open standards like OpenTelemetry and Prometheus so customers aren't locked into a single vendor, with a particular focus on Kubernetes and the open-source observability community. And AI runs through both what we build and how we build it: we use AI to surface insights, let customers interrogate their data conversationally, and investigate root cause, while also building the observability layer for AI itself, covering the agents, inference endpoints, and training jobs customers now run in production.

We work differently from many product teams, largely because AI has changed what a PM can do directly. Our PMs design their own products rather than handing off to designers, build their own prototypes rather than specifying them in documents, and pull their own data rather than queuing for analyst time. That shortens the loop between an idea and customer feedback considerably. As an intern on a small team, you'll see firsthand how the role is evolving, and you'll own a problem end to end.

Key job responsibilities
As a Sr. PMT MBA intern, you will own multiple projects in the AWS observability space from start to finish. You will:

Find and define customer problems in how teams monitor, troubleshoot and operate cloud-native applications

Design and build working prototypes yourself, and use them to test ideas with customers

Work with engineers to turn what your ideas into a product vision, requirements and a roadmap

Work with the open-source community (for example, projects like OpenTelemetry and Prometheus) to understand where it is going and find ways for AWS to contribute

Use AI and data to make decisions and measure customer and business impact

Present your recommendations to senior leaders at the end of the internship


A day in the life
This role suits someone highly autonomous and self-driven. You decide what matters most, set your own direction, and move things forward. AI is how you'll do most of it: synthesizing customer interviews, querying telemetry data, drafting the PRD, building the prototype. One day you might interview a customer running Kubernetes at scale in the morning, have a working prototype by the afternoon, and review it with engineers before you log off — work that used to take a quarter and three other people. Experienced Principal PMs will mentor you, but you own your work and its outcomes from day one.

The team is growing, so strong performers may be considered for a full-time role in 2028.

AWS is hiring a Network Development Engineer to join our MONA team.

MONA builds and operates the management plane, out-of-band (OOB) network, and automation systems that keep AWS's global network running. We use software and AI, not manual process, to solve problems that people, runbooks, and tickets have solved until now.

As a Network Development Engineer in Dublin, you'll work on several Senior Leadership initiatives at once. They include One Management Network, the next generation of how we build management connectivity across the fleet; faster on-site server builds; Initial Access, our new satellite-based product that supports multiple organizations in parallel and cuts the time to bring a new data center online; and support for new EC2 and security requirements. You'll join a team of network and software engineers working side by side, and you'll build and own pieces of this work from design through to launch. We want engineers who see a recurring network problem and build a product to solve it, not just a fix.

Key job responsibilities
Network Development Engineers in MONA build and operate the software and network systems that manage AWS's global network. You will design, deploy, scale, and sustain management plane, out-of-band, and automation platforms. You will use AI to troubleshoot and automate network operations, and you will write the documentation that lets others run what you build.

- Design, build, and operate production automation and controller software that detects, diagnoses, and remediates network faults without manual intervention.
- Use AI to automate repetitive operational work. Identify recurring network problems and turn them into reusable products, tools, and agentic workflows instead of one-off fixes, runbooks, or tickets.
- Own projects from design through to operation in areas such as device management, out-of-band connectivity, Initial Access, network deployment and scaling, technology refresh, and sustaining engineering.
- Make and implement changes on the network safely, using tooling, testing, and staged rollouts.
- Work closely with software engineering and automation teams to define the tools and controllers that let us scale to a much larger fleet with a smaller team.
- Use AI to troubleshoot network issues faster. Work with the highest-tier escalation engineers and resolvers, and drive root cause analysis and corrective actions through to completion.
- Troubleshoot routing, interconnectivity, platform, performance, and configuration issues from Top of Rack to the network border. This includes low-level application behaviour, Unix systems, and modern network software tooling.

- Maintain standards across the network toolset, and ensure our systems comply with those standards and policies.
- Use operational data to find the largest sources of manual work and device downtime, and prioritise engineering effort against them, including out-of-service targets.
- Deliver simple, sustainable, and repeatable solutions and processes. Convert standard operating procedures and runbooks into automated, AI-driven workflows, with guardrails, validation, and human review where the risk calls for it.
- Take part in on-call, and reduce its load by cutting alarm noise and using AI and automation to handle common responses.
- Write and review design documents, operational procedures, runbooks, and knowledge transfer material. Use AI to draft and update this material, and check it for accuracy before it is used.


About the team
MONA sits inside AWS Network Fabric Engineering (NFE) and owns the management plane, out-of-band networks, and automation that keep AWS's global network running. Our work is moving from keeping that growth operable to redesigning the control layer beneath it, using software and AI to replace manual process.

Our team builds the data platforms at the core of Amazon, storing customer orders, catalog and product information, shopping carts, device data, and hundreds of other business-critical datasets. The performance and availability of our platform is critical to the reliability of the Amazon brand, and we run some of the largest fleets and highest-throughput services at the company.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II who understands distributed systems at scale and wants to shape the shared storage layer of our next-generation online transaction processing (OLTP) database. You will design how committed transactions are materialized to cloud object storage, how space is reclaimed as data is superseded, and how data nodes read back through a storage-format-agnostic contract. You will partner with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to leverage cloud-native technologies and contribute innovations back to the broader market. If you thrive on solving ambiguous, high-impact problems from design to delivery, we would love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
* Design, develop, and operate the distributed shared storage layer that holds the durable copy of every committed write for Amazon's mission-critical OLTP database platform.
* Collaborate with Senior Engineers and peers to define technical solutions for complex problems such as storage engine design, durability and consistency protocols, read-path caching, and backpressure under load.
* Own end-to-end delivery of features, from writing design documents and implementing production-quality code to driving operational readiness and deployment.
* Mentor engineers through design and code reviews, pairing on hard problems, and helping them take on larger pieces of the system while raising the team's quality bar.
* Build monitoring, alarming, and automation that keep our high-throughput services reliable, and participate in on-call rotations to troubleshoot issues and drive root-cause resolution.

A day in the life
You will split your time between deep individual work like writing code, reviewing designs, and prototyping storage-layer changes, and collaborative sessions with your team and partner teams. Expect regular design reviews where you debate trade-offs around durability, latency, and cost, along with weekly operational reviews that keep the platform healthy. Some weeks you will be heads-down implementing a new compaction strategy; other weeks you will pair with a teammate to debug a subtle consistency issue in production.

About the team
Our team sits within the Transact organization and is responsible for the storage engine layer that underpins Amazon's OLTP platform that powers all Amazon Stores. We are a group of engineers who care deeply about correctness, performance, and operational rigor. We partner closely with AWS service teams, sharing innovations in both directions. Our focus over the coming years is scaling the next-generation storage layer to meet Amazon's growing transaction volume while improving efficiency and reducing costs, and we are looking for engineers who want to help shape that future.

As a Software Development Engineer on Amazon CloudWatch Alarms, you will design and operate the service that continuously evaluates customer metrics and logs, and acts on them in real time — notifying on-call teams, scaling fleets, and recovering resources, often while the rest of a customer's infrastructure is under stress. When our customers have an incident, our alarms have to be right and on time — that is the problem you will work on every day.

CloudWatch is the observability service of Amazon Web Services (AWS), used by developers, site reliability engineers (SREs), system operators, and IT managers to monitor their applications and infrastructure. CloudWatch processes quadrillions of metric observations every month and continuosly evaluates millions of alarms, with tight latency and correctness requirements.

This role is based in Dublin, Ireland.

Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Design, build and operate highly available distributed systems that evaluate customer alarms and trigger notifications and automated actions across AWS.

Deliver new alarming capabilities — from composite alarms to anomaly detection — from design through launch in every AWS Region.

Dive deep into operational issues, identify root causes, and put fixes in place that prevent them from recurring.

Collaborate with partner teams across CloudWatch and AWS to turn customer requirements into designs and incremental, safe deliverables.

Mentor junior engineers and share what you learn through design and code reviews.

A day in the life
You might start the day investigating why a customer's alarm changed state later than expected, then join a design review for a new capability that lets customers monitor thousands of resources with a single alarm. In the afternoon, you could profile the evaluation path to cut latency and cost. AI coding assistants and agents are part of how you work every day — you'll use them to explore unfamiliar code, prototype ideas, write tests, and speed up investigations, freeing up more of your time for design and hard problems.

This role includes participating in an on-call rotation for the services the team owns. We don't like getting paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we build our systems to be fault tolerant. When we do get paged, we work together to resolve the root cause so we don't get paged for the same issue twice.

About the team

When our customers have an incident, our alarms have to be right and on time — that is the problem you will work on every day.

CloudWatch is the observability service of Amazon Web Services (AWS), used by developers, site reliability engineers (SREs), system operators, and IT managers to monitor their applications and infrastructure. CloudWatch processes quadrillions of metric observations every month and continuosly evaluates millions of alarms, with tight latency and correctness requirements.

This role is based in Dublin, Ireland.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Design, build and operate highly available distributed systems that evaluate customer alarms and trigger notifications and automated actions across AWS.

Deliver new alarming capabilities — from composite alarms to anomaly detection — from design through launch in every AWS Region.

Dive deep into operational issues, identify root causes, and put fixes in place that prevent them from recurring.

Collaborate with partner teams across CloudWatch and AWS to turn customer requirements into designs and incremental, safe deliverables.

Mentor junior engineers and share what you learn through design and code reviews.

You might start the day investigating why a customer's alarm changed state later than expected, then join a design review for a new capability that lets customers monitor thousands of resources with a single alarm. AI coding assistants and agents are part of how you work every day — you'll use them to explore unfamiliar code, prototype ideas, write tests, and speed up investigations, freeing up more of your time for design and hard problems.

This role includes participating in an on-call rotation for the services the team owns. jobs.description_text: By clicking the “Apply” button, I understand that my employment application process with Takeda will commence and that the information I provide in my application will be processed in line with Takeda’s  Privacy Notice  and  Terms of Use .  I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.       Job Description      SUMMARY:    The Environmental, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHSS) Auditor conducts EHSS audits to verify adherence to internal technical standards, regulatory requirements and to confirm that management systems, including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001, are maintained effectively.  The role identifies internal EHSS risks, determines their severity and escalates them through the relevant governance channels. It advises business functions through support, verification and challenge so that risks are mitigated. It also supports continuous improvement by sharing lessons learned, insights and trends that strengthen internal controls.        DETAILED ACCOUNTABILITIES:         Leads EHSS audits in accordance with the EHSS audit program and in alignment with the global audit standard and corporate EHS audit manual, working with direction from the EHS Auditor & Program Lead and the Head of Enterprise Operational Risk Audits.  Plan, develop and deliver audits as assigned   Provide input into the annual audit schedule and long-range audit plan and objectives.  Contributes to the EHSS audit program roadmap strategy by supporting the generation and consolidation of audit data, identifying trends and communicating these effectively to relevant stakeholders.  Support and drive continuous improvement of the audit approach and audit program.  Ensures the timely delivery and communication of CAPAs and post-audit trending.  Support, as requested, the external risk and sustainability due diligence and audit program, including participation in third-party assessments and the reporting of results.  Actively identifies and implements innovative digital solutions to evolve the program into a dynamic, intelligence-led audit program. Leverages AI and technology to streamline and front-load the audit process.  Reports audit program outcomes to the EHS Auditor & Program Lead and Head of Enterprise Operational Risk Audits and develop insights to support the escalation of risks through the enterprise risk management process and other escalation channels, as appropriate, including contributing to the Management Review process of the corporate EHS management system.           Technical Expertise          Expert EHS auditor with broad understanding of EHS technical programs and how they contribute to achieving risk mitigation.    Expert understanding of relevant management system standards, including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001.  Broad knowledge of international EHS-related regulation, including national and regional specificities.  Understanding and demonstrable experience in leveraging digital solutions to streamline and create efficiencies in the audit approach.  Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks and assess priorities effectively.      Leadership skills      A high degree of integrity, authority and a respectful and collaborative approach are integral for success in this role.  A respectful and reasoned communicator with a strong ability to lead through influencing, managing change and resolving conflict.  Ability to direct the audit function and external consultants, with confidence in interacting with regulatory authorities and certification bodies.  Ability to apply sound judgment, especially during adverse findings and risk escalation, and have the courage and conviction to speak up when needed.      Decision-making and Autonomy      Ability to make decisions about complex EHS situations considering objectives, risks, implications, and agency and governmental regulations.  Utilizes information from multiple sources, solicits and considers feedback from partners and other stakeholders before making decisions, and considers all available options.  Actively engages relevant stakeholders across the business when required, with strong escalation judgment.     EDUCATION, BEHAVIORAL COMPETENCIES , SKILLS:         Essential:    Bachelor’s degree in engineering, life science, environmental science, occupational health and safety, sustainability or a related field.  6+ years’ experience in EHSS, predominately as an auditor either internally or as a consultant.  EMS or OHMS lead auditor certification or able to get certification within 6 months.  Expert knowledge of EHS management systems (ISO 14001, ISO 45001, PSM, etc.) and technical topics (health, safety, and environmental compliance).  Wide range of audit experience in the USA, EU and Japan, with knowledge of laws and regulations in these regions.  Experienced and proficient at working in a global matrixed organization.  Highly proficient with digital technologies.     Desired:    At least 5+ years’ experience within a highly regulated industry, such as biopharmaceuticals, chemicals, refining or nuclear.  Certification in sustainability assurance such as ISSA 5000 or similar.  Certified Professional EHS Auditor (CPEA) certification  Demonstrable use of AI to create audit efficiencies.           ADDITIONAL INFORMATION     Travel: Travel is an essential requirement of this role: 40%; domestic and international.     Location:  Dublin, or co-located at ant Takeda manufacturing site in Europe or Asia.   In general, the position requires a combination of sedentary work and walking around observing conditions in facilities, including controlled environments requiring gowning and personal protective clothing over the head, face, hands, feet and body and lifting up to 20Kg.Flexibility to engage in work activities outside of the normal 8-hour workday and across time zones.     Locations  IRL - Dublin - Baggot Street    Base Salary Range:  €84,800.00 - €116,600.00  The estimated salary range reflects an anticipated range for this position. Serve as a senior communications counselor to IBU Inflammation business leaders, providing strategic guidance on major milestones, key external events, reputational opportunities, issues management and stakeholder engagement.
